title: Head of Cards Portfolio Management I S4 I Cards & Payments I Milton Keynes I Internal Mobility
description:
Head of Cards Portfolio Management I S4 I Cards & Payments I Milton Keynes I Internal MobilityCountry: United Kingdom

IT STARTS HERE


Santander () is evolving from a global, high-impact brand into a technology-driven organisation, and our people are at the heart of this journey. Together, we are driving a customer-centric transformation that values bold thinking, innovation, and the courage to challenge what’s possible.


This is more than a strategic shift. It’s a chance for driven professionals to grow, learn, and make a real difference.


Our mission is to contribute to help more people and businesses prosper. We embrace a strong risk culture and all our professionals at all levels are expected to take a proactive and responsible approach toward risk management.


Retail & Commercial Banking is a global business integrating all our retail and commercial banking activities to better serve our customers, improve efficiency and drive value creation.


THE DIFFERENCE YOU MAKE


Santander UK is looking for a Head of Cards Portfolio Management based out of Milton Keynes.


This is a unique opportunity at the heart of a rapidly scaling Cards business. You’ll lead the commercial and customer performance of Santander UK’s Cards portfolio with clear accountability for sustainable, risk adjusted growth within the existing debit and credit card book. Reporting to the Head of Cards & Payments Proposition, the role is a key member of the Cards leadership team, owning portfolio strategy and lifecycle optimisation.


Success will mean delivering growth in portfolio profitability, customer engagement, card usage and retention whilst achieving consistently good customer outcomes in collaboration with the wider Cards business, Credit Risk, Finance, Marketing, Technology and Digital teams.


As part of a Global Cards business, you’ll work closely with Global Cards leadership, bringing energy, curiosity and strong commercial judgement to turn opportunities into action and help shape the next phase of our growth journey.

Key Responsibilities


We’re shaping the way we work through innovation, cutting-edge technology, collaboration and the freedom to explore new ideas. To succeed in this role, you will


  • Own commercial performance for the existing cards portfolio including income, balances, spend, customer yields, back book pricing, risk adjusted returns and delivery against budget.
  • Grow customer value and share of wallet by increasing card usage, spend, balances and top-of-wallet behaviour.
  • Strengthen engagement, loyalty and retention, creating compelling reasons for customers to choose and stay with Santander.
  • Improve existing customer experience and NPS, using insight and feedback to strengthen communications, servicing and partnering with Cards Acquisition on proposition development.
  • Lead portfolio and lifecycle management, optimising portfolio pricing, credit limits, customer journeys and customer segment led treatments.
  • Have joint accountability with Credit Risk to manage credit quality, affordability, impairment, portfolio monitoring and remediation decisions.
  • Deliver good customer and regulatory outcomes, including Consumer Duty, persistent debt and support for customers in financial difficulty.
  • Lead a high-performing Cards Portfolio team of 5 colleagues and a cross-functional agenda, collaborating with Cards Acquisition and Servicing Teams, Cards Global team, Finance, Risk, Analytics, Digital, Marketing and Operations to turn opportunities into results.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING


Our people are our greatest strength. Every individual contributes unique perspectives that make us stronger as a team and as an organisation. We’re enabling teams to go beyond by valuing who they are and empowering what they bring.


The following requirements represent the knowledge, skills, and abilities essential for success in this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


Professional Experience


  • Significant credit cards experience, with a strong understanding of card economics, portfolio management and customer behaviour. (Required)
  • Proven P&L and commercial leadership, including portfolio segmentation, pricing/yield optimisation, balance-sheet management and risk-adjusted returns. (Required)
  • Experience developing and executing portfolio and lifecycle strategies including customer segmentation, retention and customer treatments. (Preferred)
  • Strong understanding of credit risk and regulatory governance, including affordability, impairment, Consumer Duty and responsible lending. (Required)
  • Track record of delivering material customer and commercial change in complex cross-functional environments. (Required)
  • Senior leadership experience leading high performing teams and influencing stakeholders across functions to deliver in an agile way. (Preferred)

Education


  • Degree or equivalent professional experience in Business, Economics, Finance, Marketing, or a related discipline. (Preferred)
  • Professional qualifications relating to Product Management, Marketing, Banking or Financial Services. (Preferred)
  • MBA, CIM qualification or other relevant advanced professional qualification. (Preferred)

Languages


  • English business communication skills, both written and verbal. (Required)

Skills & Capabilities


  • Commercial and strategic leadership – strong proposition and portfolio management capability, balancing long-term strategy with near-term commercial performance and customer outcomes. (Required)
  • Highly analytical and data-driven – able to interpret complex customer, financial and market data to identify opportunities and make clear commercial decisions.(Required)
  • Strong financial capability – experienced in business cases, financial analysis and translating insight into actions that improve portfolio performance and returns.(Required)
  • Senior leadership and influence – able to lead teams, navigate complex organisational structures and mobilise stakeholders around shared outcomes.(Required)
  • Executive communication and challenge – able to simplify complex issues, present compelling recommendations and constructively challenge and influence senior decision-makers.(Required)
  • Curious, customer-focused and adaptable – commercially minded, comfortable operating at pace and through ambiguity, with a strong focus on innovation and continuous improvement.(Required)

WE VALUE YOUR IMPACT


At Santander, your contribution matters. We recognise the difference you make every day, and we make sure you feel valued, supported and rewarded in return.


Here, recognition goes beyond pay. It’s about the pride you feel in your work, the impact you have on customers and communities, and the opportunities you have to grow and thrive — personally and professionally.


Salary Range:
£74,144.00 - £111,216.00 per annum (depending on experience)


This salary range represents the expected remuneration for the role. Annual salary is based on a standard 35-hour working week. Actual salary offered will depend on skills, experience, qualifications and location.

  • Competitive rewards that reflect the real impact you make and the value you bring.
  • Wellbeing that goes beyond work — we work with a range of wellbeing partners across our 4 pillars of wellbeing (physical, mental, social and financial) to give you access to a suite of apps, discounted gym and fitness access, weekly online classes, flexible healthcare and mental health support.
  • Support for every life stage — from menopause and pregnancy to parenthood and beyond, with enhanced family leave, childcare options and tailored wellbeing support.
  • Time to give back through volunteering opportunities that let you make a difference in the communities we serve.
  • Global growth opportunities to shape your career, learn new skills and explore what’s possible across our international network.

Ready to be recognised? It starts with you.

LOCAL COMPLIANCE


At Santander, we’re proud to be an inclusive organisation that provides equal opportunities for everyone — regardless of age, gender, disability, civil status, race, religion or sexual orientation.


We’re committed to creating a recruitment experience that’s accessible, fair and welcoming for all candidates.


We want our people to thrive — at work and at home — while delivering the best outcomes for our customers and supporting each other to grow.


To make this possible, our roles are site-based with a hybrid working pattern, where colleagues are expected to attend the office at least 12 days per month (pro-rata for part-time roles).


When applying, please consider the travel distance, time and cost to your chosen office location(s).


We welcome applications on the understanding that, should you be offered this role, there may be no relocation package available. Santander will pay the employer mandatory government fees that are required to pay in connection with visa sponsorship. You may be liable for your own personal employee immigration and relocation costs


IMPORTANT INFORMATION FOR INTERNAL APPLICANTS:


If you are currently employed by Santander UK plc on TSB Legacy terms or by TSB and choose to apply for this Santander vacancy, please be aware that, if successful, you will move onto full Santander terms and conditions of employment and will no longer be part of the TSB Legacy population with effect from the start date of your new role.

WHAT TO DO NEXT

If this sounds like a role you are interested in, then please apply.

For further Guidance please visit Internal Mobility - Candidate Guidance.

If you want to know more about the opportunity:

Please contact Kiran Abrar

Email: Kiran.Abrar@santander.co.uk

Du har körkort & tillgång till egen bil.

Du kommer att marknadsföra multimaskinen Clear Sky Touch, ett av världens mest hälsosamma luftreningssystem. Man kan även skura golv, putsa fönster, kemtvätta helt utan kemikalier, mm. Gå gärna in på vår hemsida och läs mer.

Du får ett schema som är anpassat efter dina önskemål, som du kan med fördel kombinera med dina fritidsintressen, familj och vänner. Då besöken är förbokade känner du dig alltid välkommen dit du kommer.

Bifoga CV och ditt personliga brev i din ansökan!

Mycket goda kunskaper i svenska i tal och skrift är ett krav, då det är en nödvändighet för det dagliga arbetet i tjänsten.

Ansökningarna bearbetas löpande och för den som är tillgänglig redan nu finns möjligheten att matchas mot uppdrag omgående. Välkommen med din din ansökan redan idag!


Produkten

Världshälsoorganisationen (WHO) uppskattar att mer än en byggnad av fyra har problem med inomhusluftkvalitet. Inomhusluften är mer förorenad än utomhusluften (5 till 100 gånger, US EPA). Luftföroreningar inomhus rankas som en hög prioriterad hälsorisk - det är rankat på 5:e plats som en orsak till ohälsa i världen (WHO). 90% av vår tid spenderar vi inomhus.


Clear Sky Touch är en unik kvalitetsprodukt med en av marknadens bästa garantier och är en portabel luftrenare med flera funktioner. Den har funnits på marknaden i över 25 år och säljs idag i 49 länder över hela världen.

title: Influencer Director
description:
Please note that we will never request payment or bank account information at any stage of the recruitment process. As we continue to grow our teams, we urge you to be cautious of fraudulent job postings or recruitment activities that misuse our company name and information. Please protect your personal information during any recruitment process. While Monks may contact potential candidates via LinkedIn, all applications must be submitted through our official website ().

About the Role

We are seeking an Influence Director to spearhead and grow the influencer marketing business for Monks Paris. As the external face of our local Influence expertise, you will embody our vision at keynotes, industry events, and high-stakes client meetings. This role is a critical growth engine for the French market. You will lead a Paris-based team of 5, driving operational excellence and collaborating on select EMEA-wide projects and solutions.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead, mentor, and foster a collaborative culture for the Paris-based team; secure, and streamline internal workflows to reliably execute increasingly large-scope projects featuring hundreds of influencers simultaneously.
  • Oversee the selection, evaluation, and transition of influencer marketing platforms and tech tools used by the local team, collaborating with international counterparts
  • Act as the external ambassador for Monks’ Influence offering in France, representing the agency at public events, keynotes, and industry panels, while acting as the strategic lead on complex, high-budget pitches.
  • Provide top-tier strategic support to major local and global accounts, ensuring innovative creator strategies drive measurable business growth.
  • Partner closely with Parisian cross-functional teams (Operations, Strategy, Creative, Data, and Paid Media) to build robust, integrated connections and to plan strategies that bridge owned, earned, and paid media.
  • Coordinate with the wider EMEA network to help standardize local scopes and processes, ensuring Paris benefits from and contributes to regional best practices.
  • Educate and advocate for the Paris team’s latest solutions and operational successes to leadership and account leads, unlocking organic upsell opportunities within existing portfolios.
  • Design and lead workshops with partner platforms, clients, and content creators to leverage emerging social trends, performance tools, and content dynamics for new commercial products.

About You

The essentials:

  • 7–10+ years of experience spanning social media strategy, strategic planning, and dedicated influencer marketing management within fast-paced digital, creative, or activation agencies.
  • Proven leadership track record, with experience managing multi-level teams (including senior and junior profiles) and driving local market growth.
  • Deep experience managing large-scale, high-volume creator campaigns, with a sharp eye for legal, financial, and operational workflows.
  • Highly confident in external-facing environments, with the charisma and communication skills required to command a room at keynotes, industry events, or C-level client presentations.
  • Strong understanding of how influence intersects with paid media amplification, social data analytics, and overall brand strategy.
  • Bilingual fluency in French and English is mandatory, as you will navigate the local Parisian ecosystem while seamlessly connecting with our international network.

At Monks, we believe in fostering an environment where a diversity of perspectives can thrive. We proactively work to design hiring processes that promote equity and inclusion while mitigating bias. We celebrate diversity and are committed to building a team that reflects the communities we serve. We welcome and encourage qualified applicants, from all backgrounds, who are excited to contribute to our mission.

#LI-FP1

About Monks

Monks is the global, digital-first, data-driven, unitary operating brand of S4Capital plc, where our culture centers on how we show up for the work and for one another. That begins with the commitment to strive for mastery—taking deep pride in our craft and creating work that sets the bar. In everyday execution, we drive momentum by choosing bold action rather than waiting for certainty. Above all, our teams are stronger together, bringing diverse perspectives into a unified team that communicates with clarity, trust, and mutual respect.

This commitment to craft and innovation translates directly into widespread industry acclaim: Monks was named a Contender in The Forrester Wave™: Global Marketing Services and a leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Global Digital Marketing Agencies. It ranks among Cannes Lions' Top 10 Creative Companies (2022-25) and remains the only partner featured in AdExchanger’s Programmatic Power Players list every year (2020-24). Named Adweek’s first AI Agency of the Year (2023) and The One Show’s inaugural AI Pioneer Organization (2025), Monks was also awarded Business Intelligence Group’s 2026 Excellence in Artificial Intelligence Award in the Human-Machine Interaction Team category. Additionally, Monks.Flow earned AI-based Marketing Solution of the Year at the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards and a 2026 Global Generative AI Award in the Agentic Marketing Innovation category. Finally, Monks achieved a record-breaking number of FWAs and continues to hold the most of any partner.

We are an equal-opportunity employer committed to building a respectful and empowering work environment for all people to freely express themselves amongst colleagues who embrace diversity in all respects. Including fresh voices and unique points of view in all aspects of our business not only creates an environment where we can all grow and thrive but also increases our potential to produce work that better represents—and resonates with—the world around us.

What you’ll do:

title: Assistant Vice Chancellor, Enterprise Data Architecture and Reporting
description:
Applications must be submitted no later than 11:59 p.m. CT on the day before the listed closing date.


Weekly Work Hours

40

Compensation Range

Administrator Range E11

Salary Minimum

$158,878.00 Annually

FLSA

United States of America (Exempt)

Work Location

  • All positions are considered on-site roles.
  • After six months of employment, some positions may be eligible to apply for a hybrid work arrangement based on job responsibilities, operational needs, supervisor approval, and Dallas College policy.
  • Academic (Faculty) positions require an on-campus presence, even when teaching online courses, in accordance with state law.

Position Type

Administrator

Why the Role Matters

The Assistant Vice Chancellor, Enterprise Data Architecture and Reporting serves as a key strategic leader responsible for ensuring that Dallas College's data is accurate, secure, governed, and accessible for informed decision-making. This role helps build and maintain the enterprise-wide data infrastructure that enables leaders, faculty, and staff to make data-driven decisions that support student success, operational excellence, and institutional accountability. The position also ensures the integrity of critical state, federal, and accreditation reporting that directly impacts the College's compliance and reputation.

The Impact of the Position


The impact of this role extends across the entire institution. By leading data warehousing, governance, reporting, and data quality initiatives, the Assistant Vice Chancellor helps transform data into trusted insights that guide strategic planning and resource allocation. The position establishes the standards, systems, and processes that support enterprise reporting, advances responsible use of AI and automation, and strengthens the College's ability to measure outcomes and drive continuous improvement. Success in this role will enhance institutional effectiveness and support Dallas College's mission to serve students and the community.


Why You Should Be Excited About the Opportunity

This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of enterprise data strategy at one of the largest community college systems in Texas. The successful candidate will have the chance to build a modern, enterprise-wide decision engine, lead transformational initiatives involving data governance and AI, and influence strategic decisions at the highest levels of the institution. The role offers the ability to combine technical expertise, executive leadership, innovation, and organizational change management while making a measurable impact on student outcomes and institutional success.

Position / Job Summary

The Assistant Vice Chancellor, Enterprise Data Architecture and Reporting is an enterprise leadership role responsible for ensuring Dallas College data are reliable, secure, well governed, and ready for institutional decision-making and accountability. Reporting to the Senior Associate Vice Chancellor, Strategic Research, Analytics & Effectiveness, the Assistant Vice Chancellor provides strategic and operational leadership for data warehousing, data governance, and official reporting functions. This position establishes the architecture, standards, controls, and service models that move data from source systems into trusted institutional data products; ensures timely and accurate state, federal, accreditation, and other official submissions; and advances shared definitions, stewardship, and data quality across the College. The Assistant Vice Chancellor leads technical and reporting professionals, partners closely with Information Technology and functional leaders, and remains sufficiently hands-on to guide data modeling, code review, troubleshooting, and modernization. The ideal candidate combines deep higher education reporting experience, strong technical and coding expertise, responsible use of AI and automation, and demonstrated success leading people and organizational change.


Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute an enterprise strategy and multi-year roadmap for data warehousing, governance, data quality, and official reporting aligned with Dallas College priorities.
  • Establish operating standards, service expectations, performance measures, and decision rights across data warehousing, governance, and official reporting functions.
  • Oversee the architecture, development, integration, performance, and reliability of the enterprise data warehouse and related pipelines.
  • Ensure data ingestion, transformation, modeling, testing, documentation, monitoring, and release processes produce accurate, timely, scalable, and reusable data assets.
  • Lead the College’s data governance framework, stewardship network, policies, standards, and processes in partnership with functional data owners and Information Technology.
  • Implement data-quality rules, scorecards, exception monitoring, source-system reconciliation, issue escalation, and remediation processes that make quality measurable and accountable.
  • Provide executive oversight for state, federal, accreditation, and other official reporting, including calendars, assignments, validation, approvals, certifications, corrections, and final submission.
  • Develop a responsible AI and automation roadmap to improve accuracy, speed, documentation, testing, monitoring, and staff capacity while maintaining human validation.
  • Lead, organize, coach, and evaluate leaders and staff across data warehousing, governance, and official reporting; set clear goals, roles, performance expectations, and development plans.
  • Ensure access, handling, retention, and sharing practices comply with institutional policy, FERPA, privacy requirements, cybersecurity standards, and least-privilege principles.

Minimum and Preferred – Education, Experience, and/or Certifications

Required Qualifications for Role

  • Master’s degree in information systems, computer science, data engineering, data science, analytics, institutional research, higher education administration, or a related field.
  • Eight (8) years of progressively responsible experience in data warehousing, data engineering, data governance, institutional research, analytics, or official reporting, including substantial experience in a higher education environment.
  • Five (5) years of experience leading and developing teams, including managers and/or multidisciplinary technical and reporting professionals.
  • Direct experience producing or overseeing state and federal higher education reports, with responsibility for validation, reconciliation, certification, corrections, and audit support; Texas higher education reporting experience preferred.
  • Proficiency in SQL and demonstrated proficiency in Python or another relevant programming language, with experience using modern data platforms and ETL/ELT technologies.
  • Demonstrated experience implementing data governance, metadata, lineage, stewardship, and enterprise data-quality practices.
  • Demonstrated experience using AI and automation responsibly to improve data engineering, reporting, documentation, validation, or operational processes.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively and influence decisions across diverse technical, operational, and executive groups.

Preferred Qualifications for Role

  • Doctorate degree in a related field preferred.
  • Official transcripts required.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Comprehensive knowledge of higher education data, business processes, accountability, and official reporting requirements, with an understanding of the mission and operating environment of community colleges.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of state and federal higher education reporting, including submission requirements, data definitions, edit checks, certifications, corrections, reconciliations, and audit documentation.
  • Expertise in enterprise data warehouse and architecture, dimensional and relational data modeling, data integration, metadata, lineage, and the delivery of trusted data products.
  • Advanced hands-on coding skills, particularly SQL, and proficiency with Python or another relevant programming language; ability to review code, troubleshoot complex data issues, and establish technical standards.
  • Experience with modern cloud data platforms and engineering practices, including ETL/ELT pipelines, APIs, orchestration, automated testing, source control, deployment, monitoring, and performance optimization.
  • Strong knowledge of data governance practices, including data ownership and stewardship, institutional definitions, master and reference data, metadata management, access controls, issue management, and policy development.
  • Ability to apply artificial intelligence and automation responsibly while maintaining human review, security, privacy, and accountability.
  • Strong strategic planning, portfolio management, change leadership, vendor management, project execution, and cross-functional communication skills.

Work Condition Environment / Physical Requirements

Normal physical job functions performed within a standard office environment. Reasonable accommodation(s) may be made to individuals with physical challenges to perform the essential duties and responsibilities.


Position Disclosure

The intent of this job description is to provide a representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities performed by incumbents of this position. Incumbents may be requested to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically presented in this description. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Position requires regular and predictable attendance.

About Us

Since 1965, Dallas College, formerly Dallas County Community College District, has served more than three (3) million students. Comprising seven campuses located around the Dallas/Fort Worth area, we are one of the largest community college systems in the state of Texas. We strive to be a leader in the community college space, placing students at the center of everything we do.

Dallas College is committed to cultivating an environment of opportunity and belonging for all students and employees. We recognize that the Dallas College workforce, and the diverse talent that stems from it, is directly linked to our success. We are part of an equal opportunity system that provides education and employment opportunities without discrimination on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, color, religion, national origin, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression, veteran status, pregnancy or any other basis protected under applicable law. In accordance with applicable law, Dallas College will make reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees’ religious practices and beliefs, as well as any mental health or physical disability needs. #LI-MB1

title: Clinical Specialist Dietitian
description:
Roles: Clinical Specialist Dietitian - Bank
Location: The Harborne Hospital (Birmingham), part of HCA Healthcare UK
Contract type: Bank - Hours Monday to Friday 09.00 -19.00
Pay: Bank hourly rate £29.45 per hour

We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced Clinical Specialist Dietitian to join our Bank at The Harborne Hospital, Birmingham.


We are seeking a Registered Dietitian (RD) who has expert skills and knowledge in a highly specialist field of practice and may be working with an extended scope.


As the clinical specialist will represent a clinical area as a service line specialist with a high level of experience. You will be involved with strategic planning and service delivery and advocate for resources to deliver effective high-quality nutritional care. You should have extensive clinical expertise and leadership skills, practicing according to best evidence with involvement in specialist networks and groups.


You should be qualified or currently training in a postgraduate field of advanced clinical practice.


This is a clinical role with a highly specialist workload and accountability for clinical leadership.


You will deputise for the Lead Dietitian when required. Depending on clinical need there may be a requirement for cover at other HCA sites


At The Harborne Hospital we have a very diverse patient caseload supporting people with craniotomy’s, prolonged intubation, tracheostomy, Cervical spine surgeries.


The Therapies department is an ever growing team currently consisting of 2 full time physios and 1 part time dietitian. We are supported by bank Physio’s and Dietitians as well as OT’s and SLT’s.


It is likely that opportunities for permanent positions will become available as volumes of patients increase. This would enable potential for opportunities for further growth and development with support provided from our specialist SLT’s at London sites.


At HCA UK we’re incredibly proud of our team culture. It’s this sense of connection and collaboration that allows us to deliver exceptional outcomes for our patients. But, we know that no hospital team is complete without the vital support of its bank – and now, we’re looking for people to be part of our growing Physiotherapy Bank at The Harborne Hospital


As part of our Bank you’ll have first refusal ahead of agencies on a range of shifts across our network of leading private hospitals, all of which are currently rated ‘Good’ or ‘Outstanding’ by the CQC. It’s a fantastic chance to gain exposure to one of the UKs leading private healthcare providers while retaining that all important flexibility over when and where you work. You can expect to work alongside leading consultants, expert colleagues and be recognised for the vital role you play within our team.



Above all else, we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life. It’s this guiding vision that influences everything we do at HCA UK. From the CEO to the colleagues on the floor we all have a part to play in delivering exceptional care to our patients. To others, this may just be a Bank role, but to us, you’re a valued member of our team, a team that improves lives on a daily basis.


What you’ll bring:

  • Right to work in the UK (no sponsorship supplied for Bank roles)
  • HCPC Registration
  • RD degree qualification or equivalent
  • Experience working in a hospital setting

Who are HCA UK?

Originally founded over 50 years ago by Dr Thomas Frist, HCA has gone on to become one of the world’s leading healthcare providers. In the UK, we’re one of the largest providers of privately funded healthcare and have invested over £500 million in the latest treatments, technology, techniques, medication and facilities. Being part of a large multisite, established healthcare group we offer the chance to broaden your clinical knowledge and thanks to our exceptional clinician to patient ratios, a healthy work environment that gives you more time to do what you do best: care.


We believe that by caring for our employees, we empower them to provide exceptional care for our patients. That’s why we offer a host of flexible benefits that reflect the invaluable contribution they make every day. Please request a copy of the Bank Benefits booklet for more details on the fantastic benefits you would access to when you join the Bank,.


Culture and values

At HCA UK we believe exceptional care starts with our people. We celebrate the unique perspectives and different experiences each of us bring as we know that when you feel seen, heard and supported you can be at your best for our patients, and each other.


Our mission is simple, above all else we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life, a clear statement that extends to both our patients and colleagues. To achieve this, we live and breathe four core values:

  • Unique and Individual: We recognise and value everyone as unique and individual
  • Kindness and compassion: We treat people with kindness and compassion
  • Honesty, integrity and fairness: - We act with absolute honesty, integrity and fairness
  • Loyalty, respect and dignity: We trust and treat one another as valued members of the HCA UK family with loyalty, respect and dignity

Reasonable adjustments

We believe everyone should feel comfortable to bring their full self to work and be afforded the same opportunities. As a Disability Confident committed organisation, we’re happy to discuss flexible working arrangements to suit your needs as well as offer reasonable adjustments throughout our recruitment process, and in the workplace, to anyone that needs them.

title: Delivery Operations Lead - Business Growth (Maternity Cover)
description:
Innovate UK has the following secondment opportunity available for employees of Innovate UK Business Connect:

Applications must be submitted by

14-10-2026

Vacancy for Delivery Operations Lead – Business Growth (Maternity Cover)


This role is part of the senior team within the Innovate UK Business Growth Team reporting to the Head of Operations & Impact and overseeing the operational delivery and fit with the wider Innovate UK group and responsible for mobilising our data as a strategic asset.


*Please note this advert will close on the 13th of October 2026 at 23.59pm.

Watch our video “Why Join Innovate UK?” here.


Title: Delivery Operations Lead – Business Growth (Maternity Cover)

Band: UKRI Band F (UKRI Ts & Cs)

Salary: £58,589 gross per annum

Reports to: Head of Operations & Impact – Business Growth

Location: UKRI sites: Swindon, London, Harwell, Daresbury, Keyworth, Cambridge, Edinburgh

Contract: Fixed Term (Extended maternity cover, 18 months c. asap – Feb 2028)


Employees applying for any opportunity which may mean being away from your substantive role for a temporary period of time, please refer to the Recruitment Policy for further information in the first instance. If you are made an offer, please ensure you liaise with your Line Manager and the designated HR Team as soon as possible in order that implications of any move are clear and understood, prior to a move taking place.


Innovate UK works with businesses and stakeholders across every nation and region of the UK. As part of UKRI, our hybrid working approach is built around one simple principle: time should be spent where it delivers the greatest impact.

This means working across three settings: UKRI sites, time on the ground with businesses, partners and stakeholders and time working from home. It's an approach designed to support collaboration, connection and impact.

This role is in Tier 2, with 40-60% of working time typically spent either at a UKRI site or engaging with external businesses and stakeholders across the UK. Outside of this requirement, you can work from home. Whilst this role will be formally based at one of the following UKRI sites, it is externally facing, and we expect that there will be requirement to travel around the UK for 2/3 days each week on average.

Read the full UKRI Hybrid Working Policy Hybrid Working at UKRI

Innovate UK recognises the importance of work-life balance and we will be happy to discuss any requests for flexible working arrangements.

Context:

The role holder will operate within the Innovate UK Business Growth Team, which sits within the Director of Business Growth & Global’s team.


Innovate UK Business Growth is a key part of the UK innovation agency’s investment in the innovative businesses that drive economic growth. Innovate UK is being reshaped to provide an integrated, end-to-end offer built around the needs of each business, not a one-size-fits-all intervention.


Innovate UK Business Growth is remaining part of the offer, engaging in the development of Velocity and continuing to provide expert growth support, mentoring, strategic advice and hands-on guidance from people who understand the technology and the market.


Job Purpose:

The ‘Delivery Operations Lead - Business Growth (Maternity Cover)’ post will form part of the senior team within the Innovate UK Business Growth Team, reporting to the Head of Operations & Impact; overseeing the operational delivery and fit with the wider Innovate UK group and responsible for mobilising our data as a strategic asset. The postholder will work closely with the other Delivery Operations Lead, other parts of the Business Growth team, and a range of internal Innovate UK & UKRI stakeholders (e.g. domain teams, operations, IUK IT, governance, compliance, legal) to ensure relevant interfaces and interdependencies are managed effectively.


In addition, the role will oversee the development of the Innovate UK Business Growth CRM and its integration with other data/survey tools (e.g. Survey MonkeyÔ, GROWTHmapperÔ, Beauhurst); data collection, management and quality assurance, including the provision of guidance and training; the development of reporting processes, dashboards and outputs that demonstrate our impact; the handling and consistent response to data requests; management of our current external evaluation; the smooth operation and improvement of Innovate UK beneficiary triage process through which Innovate UK award holders are offered business growth support; and handling of complaints, and working with Innovate UK Business Growth consortium partners, domains teams and the Innovate UK and UKRI complaints teams.


The role will also work closely with the Business Growth Team’s Innovation Leads and Service Design Leads to ensure delivery of the Business Growth service is accurately captured by the data collected and the impact of the Innovate UK Business Growth portfolio is captured, communicated and reported to key stakeholders, both internally and externally. The ‘Delivery Operations Lead - Business Growth (Maternity Cover)’ will also support the Deputy Director - Business Growth in harnessing our data as a strategic asset.


The role holder is currently responsible for managing three direct reports. A key part of the role is therefore the effective line management of the team which consists of two Impact and Performance Managers and a Senior Data Analyst.


Key Responsibilities and Accountabilities:

  • Day-to-day portfolio management of the Business Growth service, working closely with the wider Business Growth team for adviser CRM/data capability development, data management and impact measurement and reporting.
  • Management and development of our CRM, its data and the generation of accurate, relevant, and timely reporting to enable progress to be tracked centrally, including the provision of concise commentary targeted to meet EMT and external stakeholder needs.
  • Oversee the embedding of monitoring, evaluation, and impact/benefits realisation for Innovate UK’s Business Growth Support.
  • Hold the Business Growth team’s relationship with IUK IT, including engaging with and representing Business Growth requirements on the Janus and Single Customer View projects.
  • Support the development of Velocity as required, including providing an account and data management perspective.
  • Line management responsibility for our Impact and Performance Managers and Senior Data Analyst, supporting their development and developing a high-performing team and with other members of the senior team sharing best practice and mentoring other members of the wider Business Growth team.
  • Stakeholder management across a complex and diverse partner and stakeholder network, including regular, appropriate and timely communications, including effective management of relationships with internal and external suppliers, including co-chairing our consortium Data Excellence Community of Practice.
  • Delivery of process improvements and resource efficiencies as needed.
  • Support the other Delivery Operations Lead to develop and implement programme governance and effective co-ordination of all the partners within the wider offer and interfacing with the Consortium, Operations and Advisory Board as directed.
  • Ad-hoc delivery of senior-level project work as directed by the Head of Operations and Impact and/or Business Growth Deputy Director.
  • Represent the Head of Operations and Impact and Business Growth Deputy Director as required at events and meetings, acting as a delegate during periods of absence as required.

This is not an exhaustive list and you might be encouraged to undertake any other duties across the wider directorate, commensurate with the Band and level of responsibility of this post, for which the post holder has the key experience and/or training.

Shortlisting criteria

(S) – Assessed at shortlisting

(I) – Assessed at interview

(S&I) – Assessed at both shortlisting and interview

Person Specification:

  • This effective and proactive individual will be an exceptional and experienced programme manager, used to working without close direction, provide effective line management and able to manage multiple streams of work, with multiple teams.
  • The post-holder will be capable of identifying the right approach to the challenge in hand and translating that approach into effective delivery.
  • Able to develop and maintain effective working relationships with senior people across the breath of UKRI, the innovation ecosystem and relevant government departments as well as with non-governmental stakeholders.

Experience & Qualifications:

Essential –

  • Educated to undergraduate degree level or equivalent professional experience, line management experience, and with experience in a management function/role within a business support, innovation, economic development or similar environment. (S)
  • Experience of working in and developing complex networks with multiple stakeholders, building productive relationships and influencing senior stakeholders across multiple organisations where priorities and objectives may conflict, using strong communication (written and verbal), negotiation and presentation skills. (S&I)
  • Considerable experience of managing programmes and delivering a broad range of benefits, across the Public and Private sectors and the ability to translate strategic objectives into operational delivery plans with high attention to detail. (S&I)
  • Experience of developing and motivating a high-performing team across multiple locations to maintain a collaborative culture and efficiently deliver results through others. (S&I)
  • Experience of developing and implementing new processes, business critical changes and organisational change in live operational environments, demonstrating resilience, adaptability, analytical thinking and a commitment to continuous improvement. (S&I)
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making capability, including the ability to interpret complex information, identify key points and issues and develop creative, practical solutions. (I)
  • Demonstrable digital and data literacy, including the use of management information, data governance principles and maintaining data integrity within operational systems. (S&I)
  • Self-awareness, self-motivation and good personal resilience as well as a high level of professionalism, discretion, and tact. A robust and flexible approach with the ability to thrive in an agile/changing environment taking the initiative where required, but equally able to take instruction and deliver results against a brief and to tight deadlines and a demonstrable ability to manage and prioritise workload across multiple work streams. (I)Understanding UK government structure, its constituent agencies and brands, as well as the Devolved Nations and key UKRI partner organisations and how these interact to support business growth and innovation. (S&I)

Competencies:

All team members demonstrate compatibility with and capability against our Core Competencies such as:

Job Summary:

Under supervision and in collaboration with other health care professionals, assist in performing a variety of nursing care services for patients.

Job Responsibilities and Requirements:

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Receives patient care assignment from the registered nurse (RN) in charge. Initiates delegated tasks based on demonstrated competence in performing nursing activities for specific patient age group served.
  • Collects and documents data for the admission assessment, reassessment and/or scheduling appointments or surgeries at specific times for patient population. May document and provide appropriate data to the RN and/or LPN for analysis and validation of patient’s response to care or treatment and when significant change occurs in the patient’s condition.
  • Informs licensed nurse of any changes in patient condition/needs, of patient complaints, and of patient/significant other educational needs.
  • Stocks and maintains supplies and equipment in keeping with patient care needs and cost containment. Utilizes time and supplies economically and conscientiously.
  • Assists with delegated clerical duties such as answering telephones, relaying messages, transcription of physician orders, preparing and organizing the patient's medical record.
  • In an inpatient environment, responsibilities may also include the following: answers patients’ calls for help, takes their vital signs, and monitors their behavior and physical condition for progress or deterioration. Assists with baths, ambulating, feeding, skin care, personal and oral hygiene and making occupied and unoccupied beds. Performs dressing changes, enemas, ostomy care, toileting, turning, cough and deep breathing, catheter care, collection of biological specimens, measuring and recording intake and output of fluids.
  • In an inpatient environment, prepares patients for discharge and accompanies them upon dismissal as indicated. Orients new patients and significant others to the nursing unit.
  • In an outpatient environment, manages referrals for medical and surgical specialist appointments. Provides assistance in patient care to patients three years of age or older.
  • Works in a constant state of alertness and safe manner.
  • May perform point of care testing according to policies and procedures.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

  • Occasional lifting/carrying and pushing/pulling objects weighing 25-50 lbs.
  • Occasional lifting/moving patients.
  • Occasional use of smell to detect/recognize odors.
  • Occasional driving.

title: IT Governance & Supplier Lead
description:
The Work We Do

Teciem designs, builds, and delivers treasury and capital markets software solutions for financial institutions worldwide. We serve banks of every size and geography, offering the right setup for the right need.

Our solutions are designed to replace multiple disconnected systems with one complete, front-to-back platform, helping customers to capture trading and business opportunities quickly, clearly and with control. We cover the entire trading lifecycle, ensuring that everything - from execution to position keeping, to risk management – runs smoothly.

With decades of experience and one of the largest, most diverse client bases in the industry, we turn deep industry knowledge into software that covers most asset classes, meets complex real-world treasury and capital market's needs, and adapts as markets evolve.




Role Purpose

Owns supplier management, contractual and commercial governance, IT financial management and the Portfolio and Project Office function. Accountable for supplier continuity and contractual compliance across Enterprise IT.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the end-to-end supplier management framework across Enterprise IT, including onboarding, performance and exit.

  • Own contract and commercial governance, ensuring agreements are current, compliant and commercially sound.

  • Lead IT financial management, including budget setting, forecasting and cost control.

  • Lead the Portfolio and Project Office function, ensuring consistent delivery governance across all Enterprise IT initiatives.

  • Establish and chair supplier governance forums, tracking performance against contracted service levels.

  • Ensure supplier continuity planning is in place for all business-critical services.

  • Own the IT risk and issue register, ensuring appropriate escalation and mitigation.

  • Lead procurement activity for new supplier engagements, working with commercial and legal teams.

  • Provide portfolio-level reporting to Enterprise IT leadership, including RAG status and financial performance.

  • Ensure contractual compliance across all third-party arrangements, including data protection and security clauses.

  • Support Day 1 readiness through supplier transition planning and contractual continuity.

Key Accountabilities

  • Accountable for supplier performance and contractual compliance across Enterprise IT.

  • Accountable for the accuracy and integrity of the IT budget and financial reporting.

  • Accountable for delivery governance across the Enterprise IT portfolio.

  • Accountable for supplier continuity through Day 1 transition.

Essential Skills & Experience

  • Substantial experience leading supplier management and commercial governance within a large IT organisation.

  • Strong financial management experience, including budgeting, forecasting and cost control.

  • Proven track record leading a Portfolio or Project Management Office.

  • Experience negotiating and managing complex third-party contracts.

  • Strong risk and governance discipline, comfortable operating at executive reporting level.

  • Experience supporting supplier transition during a major transformation or carve-out.

  • Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills.

Desirable Skills

  • Experience of TSA exit or separation programme supplier management.

  • Procurement or commercial qualification.

  • Experience within a regulated financial services environment.

Qualifications

  • Relevant degree or equivalent professional experience.

  • Project or programme management qualification, for example Prince2 or MSP, desirable.

Key Stakeholders

  • Head of Enterprise IT and wider Enterprise IT leadership team.

  • Finance, Procurement and Legal functions.

  • Enterprise IT suppliers and third parties.

  • Programme governance forums and steering committees.

Success Measures

  • IT budget managed within agreed variance throughout the year.

  • Supplier performance consistently meets or exceeds contracted service levels.

  • Portfolio delivery governance in place with accurate, timely RAG reporting.

  • No material contractual or compliance breaches across the supplier base.

  • Supplier continuity confirmed and validated ahead of Day 1.




Diverse Minds, Shared Ambition

At Teciem, we believe that our strength comes from the diversity of our people. Different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences fuel our innovation and help us build solutions that truly make a difference in the world of financial technology.

We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels respected, heard, and empowered to grow. Here, you can bring your whole self to work, contribute your unique ideas, and be part of a team driven by shared ambition.

We welcome talent from all walks of life and encourage applications from individuals of all genders, races, ages, abilities, identities, and beliefs. Together, we’re shaping a culture where diversity isn’t just celebrated — it’s essential to our success.

Job Summary:

Care Partners are responsible for meeting the basic needs of patients by providing skilled levels of bedside patient care under the direction of the Registered Nurse. Care Partners also perform clerical duties necessary to the functioning of the nursing unit.

Job Responsibilities and Requirements:

POSITION ACCOUNTABILITIES AND PERFORMANCE CRITERIA (% of Time)

Essential Functions: The following are essential job accountabilities and performance criteria:

1) General Patient Care:

Criteria

A) Carries out the patient’s plan of care as it relates to the patient’s physical needs under the direction of the Registered Nurse.

B) Delivers care requiring broad knowledge of aseptic technique, medical terminology and equipment.

C) Assists nurses and physicians with procedures.

D) Maintains knowledge of and operates equipment used in patient care safely.

E) Retrieves patient care items that are not routinely available on the unit.

F) Retrieves, recovers or follows up on patient care needs.

G) Completed unit clerical duties including the coordination of designated unit activities, transcription of orders, medical record maintenance and serving as a unit receptionist.

H) Prepares rooms prior to admissions and following discharges. Completes patient’s belongings list on admission and transfer.

I) Directs prompt and courteous attention to the needs of patients, families, and visitors.

J) Rounds with purpose.

K) Engages in service recovery activities referring unusual problems to Nurse Manager/ Designate.

L) Rounds after dietary trays are passed to ensure all meals are appropriate or as required for patient satisfaction /care needs.

M) Takes appropriate action when necessary including the resolution of issues related to late or wrong trays.

N) Feeds and sets up trays as needed.

O) Recognizes needs and initiates appropriate action in regard to maintaining supplies and equipment

P) Notifies appropriate department in order to maintain a clean safe environment (housekeeping, maintenance, dietary, etc.)

Q) Functions as a resource person to co-workers, patients/families, medical staff, and ancillary personnel.

2) Safety and Comfort

Criteria

A) Correctly places restraints; observes for constriction of circulation, changes to skin integrity, adequate breathing; knows when and how to change position; provides range of motion (ROM) and skin care, toileting, and opportunities for socialization.

B) Operates Cardiac Monitor i.e.

1. On/off switch

2. Alarms/stand-by

3. Obtaining strip

4. Lead placement

3) Vital Signs/Measurement

Criteria

A) Completes Point of Care Testing as approved by hospital and competency

B) Obtains vital signs including temperature

C) Measures abdominal girth

D) Weighs patients

E) Measures intake and output

4) Mobility and Exercise:

Criteria

A) Applies Pneumatic Air Stockings / Ted Hose

B) Ambulates, turns and positions patients.

5) Respiratory Care

Criteria

A) Assists with incentive spirometry and cough / deep breath.

B) Sets up oxygen therapy such as, nasal cannula or mask as directed by Registered Nurse.

C) Monitors pulse oximetry

D) Completes tracheostomy care

E) Performs suctioning

1. Oral

2. Tracheal: When the patient is assessed by the Registered Nurse to be stable.

6) Wound Care

Criteria

A) Places patient on specialty bed

B) Performs dressing changes (sterile and clean)

C) Cares for pin care site after assessment has been completed by the Registered Nurse. Assists in monitoring that traction weights are hanging freely and in good alignment.

7) Bowel and Bladder Elimination

Criteria

A) Administers enemas

B) Performs straight catheterization. Provides catheter care.

8) Hygiene

Criteria

A) Provides:

1. Hygiene and grooming daily

2. Mouth care (including dentures) at least twice/day.

3. Fresh water at 0800, 1600, 2400 and as needed

4. Perineal care

5. Toileting

9) Specimen Collection

Criteria

A) Obtains:

1. Midstream (clean-voided) urine specimen.

2. Timed urine specimen

3. Sterile urine specimen from an indwelling catheter

4. Urine specific gravity (5 South and 5 ICU only)

5. Urine pH

6. Expectorated sputum specimens

7. Blood specimens by venipuncture

8. Stool specimens

10) Clerical

Criteria

A) Answers phone within 3 rings identifying self, title and nursing unit. Does not keep person on hold for extended periods.

B) Provides directions to physicians, hospital personnel, and visitors to patient’s room.

C) Notifies the physician and nursing staff of new patient’s arrival to unit.

D) Assists in the receiving of articles brought to the nursing unit.

E) Answers pneumatic tube promptly and returns carriers to the appropriate area.

F) Prepares a daily worksheet and confirms all appointments concerning daily work (including blood work) and updates worksheet on each shift.

G) Verifies census sheet, maintains and updates as necessary.

H) Informs Admitting Department of all transfers, discharges, admissions, room changes, and deaths through the computer. Includes disposition of appropriate paperwork.

I) Informs staff/charge nurses / nurse manager of nursing unit activities: return of patients to the floor, physician stat orders, new admissions, etc.

J) Assist nursing staff and ancillary personnel to ensure appropriate and complete specimen labels/requisition orders.

K) Reports critical lab values to appropriate personnel.

L) Initiates and completes secretarial portion of the pre-op checklist.

M) Completes the administrative data screen for all new admissions and updates daily.

N) Assists the nursing staff with paperwork involved in the patient transfer and discharge procedure to include movement of medications.

O) Gives a full report to the oncoming person. (Leaves a written report if unable to give verbal). Informs the Charge Nurse if additional orders are left for the night shift.

P) Checks patient chart periodically throughout the shift for “stat”, flagged and un-flagged orders.

Q) Checks physician orders daily for unsigned verbal/telephone orders and places appropriate flag.

R) Enters orders into the computer accurately.

S) Calls departments to order tests, procedures, and consults which cannot be ordered through the computer.

T) Transcribes orders for tests/procedures/consults onto the TESTS/PROCEDURES section of the profile.

U) Ensures labels are correctly placed on all forms

V) Transcribes medication orders to the medication administration record accurately.

W) Places all physician orders in pharmacy bin. Faxes all physician orders to pharmacy during night shift.

X) Signs orders to indicate orders were taken off with date, time, signature and title

Z) Ensures that stat and timed orders are transcribed promptly.

AA) Initiates and assembles charts

BB) Keeps chart in order; thins chart as needed and places in appropriate file.

DD) Ensures that Medical Records picks up old charts by placing them in assigned pick up area on day of discharge.

EE) Completes medical record checklist and ensures that the complete chart is sent to Medical Records within 24 hours of discharge and immediately upon patient death.

FF) Sends complete chart including thinned chart and old chart on transfer to patient.

GG) Ensures allergy, and isolation cards are posted in charts when indicated.

HH) Completes and signs secretarial portion of death summary.

11) Safety/Infection Control: Performs job in accordance with safety and infection control policies. (5,8) 5%

Criteria

A) Practices standard precautions and disposes of hazardous wastes per established guidelines.

B) Maintains a safe, clean, comfortable, and therapeutic environment for patients / families / employees in accordance to hospital standards.

1. Maintains clutter free environment.

2. Keeps personal conversations/background noise to a minimum.

3. Adheres to dress code.

10. Orientation competency (if new hire)

11. Unit Specific

E) Obtains report from Registered Nurse and informs nurse of changes in patient’s condition.

F) Communicates concerns or patient complaints to Registered Nurse and other team members as appropriate.

G) Documents all procedures and care concisely and legibly on chart forms according to chart form guidelines.

H) Identifies problems, gathers pertinent data, suggests solutions, communicates using appropriate lines of authority, and works toward problem resolution.

I) Empties soiled linen containers.

J) Works in a constant state of alertness and safe manner.

12) Service: Provides service excellence to the customers of Saint Louis University Hospital by delivering timely, high quality care in a courteous, and respectful manner. (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) 10%

Criteria

A) Demonstrates care and courtesy

1. Provides prompt, respectful, courteous service.

2.Meets physical, spiritual, psychological and emotional needs of patients and families as directed by Registered Nurse.

3. Responds to call lights promptly.

4. Apologizes for mix-up and delay.

1. Provides accurate change of shift report.

3. Shares knowledge with other departments to facilitate work flow and continuity.

D) Provides cost effect services

1. Uses resources wisely.

2. Recommends changes in practice that increases efficiency and minimizes waste.

13) Personal Accountability: Demonstrates accountability for own job performance. (6) 5%

Criteria

A) Adheres to and incorporates all customer service standards in patient care and work practices.

B) Participates in additional learning experiences to increase competence including:

1. Staff meetings

2. Mandatory in-services and educational programs

3. Evaluation of self-performance by identifying strengths and areas for improvement.

C) Assists in identifying and implementing nursing unit goals.

14) Performance Improvement (PI): Incorporates Performance Improvement into one's job performance. (6) 5%

Criteria

A) Identifies problems, participation in data collection when requested, suggests solutions, communicates using appropriate lines of authority and works toward problem resolution.

B) Participates in the performance / process improvement process.

1. Assists in developing unit based PI plan.

2. Participates in discussion of PI outcomes.

3. Collaborates in developing and implementing action plans.

C) Incorporates Performance Improvement and Commitment to Quality (C2Q) results into job performance

D) Offers suggestions for improvement of unit activities.

E) Participates in discussion of PI C2Q data outcomes.

F) Collects PI C2Q data as assigned

G) Participates in research activities on the nursing unit as appropriate.

15) Age Appropriate Care: Provides age-appropriate care to:

____Infant ___Child ____Adolescent _____Adult _____Geriatric

Criteria

A) Demonstrates knowledge and skills of normal growth & development necessary to provide services to the age of the patient served by the department.

B) Demonstrates ability to assess and interpret age specific data to identify patient needs.

C) Utilizes communication skills necessary to interpret age specific responses to service and interaction.

D) Involves family or significant other in decision making related to services provided.

E) Demonstrates ability to provide service needed for the age groups routinely served by the department assigned.

F) Position specific: Need to enter those responsibilities specific for position

16) Specialized Care: Provides specialized care to patients at high risk for injury.

(1, 2, 4, 5, 8) <1%

Criteria

A) Restraint Care

1. Initiates/evaluates alternatives to restraint prior to application.

2. Applies restraints consistent with the approved procedure.

3. Monitors and assesses patient’s response throughout the restraint period at the appropriate intervals.

4. Provides specified patient care (toileting, skin care, hydration, feeding, etc.) on a timely basis.

5. Provides for trail release and removal of restraint as soon as possible.

B) Pain Management

1. Follows pain management plan of care, e.g.: repositioning, message, immobilization, music therapy etc.

2. Reports patient complaints of pain to the nursing staff and/or physician.

C) Abuse Assessment

1. Is aware of abuse recognition criteria and incorporates it into assessments.

2. Reports signs of possible abuse/neglect to the physician & Risk Management, and recommends appropriate consultations (psychiatric, Social Work) for evaluation.

Practice Agreement

For Nursing Staff

Please read the below standards and expectations.

Standard (I understand that…)

Our patients deserve care that sets the standard for excellence and meets the needs of each and every patient whose care is our primary purpose and mission. (Quality)

Expectations (So I will…)

Achieve Excellence in Infection Control By:

  • Isolating per policy.
  • Consistently adhering to proper infection control practices and I will educate patients and visitors of the same.
  • Taking responsibility to read, learn, follow, enforce and remain up to date on Saint Louis University Hospital policies and procedures.
  • Practicing excellent hand washing technique - Wash or gel my hands when going into and coming out of patient rooms and between glove use, especial when it relates to dressing changes, suctioning, etc.
  • Change dressings when they need to be changed now rather than later and maintain all invasive lines as directed by policy.
  • Vaccinate per policy.
  • Notify my supervisor if I see anyone or anything that puts my patient at risk.
  • Utilizing safe practices during crisis situations (i.e. codes) and transport to other departments, e.g. masks, 02 tanks.

Achieve Excellence in Nursing Practice By:

  • Contributing in a positive way to the functioning of the patient care team.
  • Taking an active role in practice development through participation in unit based and hospital committees.
  • Ensuring that documentation of patient care is consistently thorough and legible.
  • Rounding with a purpose on each patient.
  • Modeling practice excellence to new employees.
  • Ensuring that licensure, certifications, and other mandatory requirements are completed within assigned deadlines.

Own and Respect My Environment By:

  • Maintaining proper care of and treat all equipment with respect (clean up after using the microwave, not hit the walls with beds etc.).
  • Maintaining a neat, clean and organized work environment.
  • Keeping the nursing station, bathroom, and break room neat and clean.
  • Leaving my patient’s room in good order, with supplies in place, and ready for the next shift and my work area in the same condition as I would like to see when I return.
  • If I see something out of order I will pick it up, fix it, or call to have it repaired. I will not assume that someone else will do it.
  • Giving hand-off report to another nurse before I leave the unit with another patient or for any other errand.

Standard (I understand that…)

Treating my colleagues, our patients, visitors, and business partners with respect and dignity is necessary to create an environment where excellence in caring and nursing practice can thrive. (People)

Expectations (So I will…)

  • Show empathy to every patient and communicate my commitment to assist in their comfort, safety, and restoration to health.
  • Demonstrate my respect to my colleagues and co-workers through effective communication about patients’ condition and concerns, mentoring new employees, resolving conflicts constructively, and proactively scheduling shifts to meet unit needs.
  • Come to work with a positive attitude.
  • Offer constructive criticism to co-workers when addressing concerns, praising in public and criticizing in private when necessary.
  • Be part of the solution – not part of the problem.
  • Not complain to or complain in front of my patients/families and staff (i.e. too busy or short staffed, no lunch).
  • Follow up on patient concerns every time to the appropriate person.
  • Respond promptly to patient requests.
  • Always refer to physicians as Dr. ____.
  • Make sure that my patients are checked at least every 01 hour 0 30 minutes 0 15 minutes per clinical standard and as appropriate.

Standard (I understand that…)

Patients and their families are scared and vulnerable. It is my responsibility to communicate through verbal and non-vernal means that I am here to help. (Service)

Expectations (So I will…)

keri.fisher@oregonstate.edu

Job Summary:

The College of Health's Center for Global Health (CGH) is seeking a Program Coordinator. This is a part-time (0.50 FTE), 12-month, professional faculty position.

The College of Health’s Center for Global Health (CGH) brings together faculty, students, and partners to advance collaborative global health education, research, and capacity-building. The Program Coordinator will play an integral role in supporting the Center for Global Health and Botswana Global Health Initiative (BGHI), contributing to programs that connect Oregon State University students and faculty with international partners and communities.

This position offers a unique opportunity to work across global health programming, education abroad, research, and partnership engagement. The Program Coordinator will help coordinate the Center’s day-to-day operations and initiatives, including OSU’s Botswana summer study program, while supporting research and capacity-building projects, communications, and relationships with local and international partners. The role is well suited for someone who enjoys managing varied projects, building relationships, and helping turn collaborative ideas into successful programs.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate day-to-day operations, projects, meetings, workshops, and training activities for the Center for Global Health and Botswana Global Health Initiative.
  • Coordinate College of Health education abroad programming, including the Botswana summer study program, student recruitment and preparation, travel logistics, risk management, and post-program activities.
  • Support the design, implementation, evaluation, and dissemination of global health research and capacity-building initiatives.
  • Contribute to grant proposals, reports, budgets, and sponsored-project administration, including tracking expenditures, timelines, deliverables, and reporting requirements. Workplan - Program Coordinator.
  • Develop and maintain program procedures, records, databases, partner agreements, participant documentation, and evaluation data.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for program partners and support communications, presentations, reports, newsletters, and other outreach materials.

Qualifications:

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:


  • Bachelor’s degree in public health, kinesiology, human development, or related field and three years of experience providing administrative support to a program or office
  • Effective communication skills and the ability to uphold the highest standards of professionalism, relationships across all levels, and with external partners.
  • Experience in planning and managing programs within the U.S. and abroad, which includes coordinating with co-workers and community partners while managing logistics and budgets.
  • Ability to maintain strict confidence with information about faculty, students, and work performed.
  • Demonstrated ability to successfully manage multiple tasks and shifting priorities within an environment with frequent interruptions.
  • Demonstrated ability to review and edit professional and scientific documents.
  • Experience supporting student workers, graduate assistants, and program participants.
  • Training and/or experience in the operation of computers and software applications (e.g., MS Word, Excel, etc.)

This position is designated as a critical or security-sensitive position; therefore, the incumbent must successfully complete a criminal history check and be determined to be position-qualified as per University Standard: 05-010 et seq. Incumbents are required to self-report convictions, and those in youth programs may have additional criminal history checks every 24 months.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:


  • Experience with community-based participatory programs.
  • Graduate degree in public health, kinesiology, human development, or related field.
  • Experience contributing to successful grant proposals or sponsored research applications (e.g., NIH, NSF, or foundation funding).
  • Demonstrated project management skills, including tracking timelines, budgets, and deliverables across multiple concurrent projects.
  • Prior experience living, studying, or working internationally.
  • Proficiency with data management or collaboration software (e.g., REDCap, Qualtrics, Microsoft Teams).
  • Experience in donor relations, fundraising, or partner communication.


Working Conditions/Schedule:

This is a campus-based position with core hours Monday through Friday. Some schedule flexibility is available with supervisor approval. The role requires occasional evening or weekend work for program events and deadlines, periodic international travel to Botswana (typically two to three weeks per trip), and occasional coordination outside standard hours with international partners.

title: Senior Appointment Setter – Australian Healthcare / Dental || Onsite
description:
About the Team You’ll Join:

Our client is a national Australian dental franchise group specializing in All-on-4 dental implant procedures. The treatment provides patients who may otherwise rely on dentures with a permanent implant-supported solution, helping them regain confidence, function and quality of life.

The business also operates a growing dentist education and training division, creating further opportunities for the offshore sales team to support lead qualification and appointment setting as the operation expands.

Our client is now establishing a dedicated offshore appointment-setting function through Outforce to improve speed-to-lead, increase lead-to-consult conversion and support significant future growth in digital marketing activity.

Job Overview:

Employment type: Full time

Shift: AU Hours

Work setup: ONSITE - The Curve, 32nd Street corner 3rd Avenue, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig City

What we offer:

  • Competitive compensation package aligned with your skills and experience

  • Comprehensive HMO coverage, including a free dependent on Day 1

  • Employee referral program with rewarding incentives

  • 20 days of annual leave, giving you flexibility to manage your time

  • Engaging team activities and events to keep work enjoyable

  • Build strong, high-impact connections with key stakeholders across the business

  • Take part in client engagement initiatives to elevate your professional experience.

Role Overview:

We are seeking experienced Senior Appointment Setters to join an initial team supporting approximately 1,000 warm patient enquiries per month.

This is not traditional cold calling.

Leads are generated through the client's marketing campaigns and the primary objective is to engage prospective patients quickly, understand their needs, qualify their suitability and confidently book them into a consultation with our client clinic.

The offshore team will allow clinic-based staff to focus on face-to-face patient consultations and clinical coordination while the appointment-setting team takes ownership of lead follow-up and conversion.

The initial team is expected to consist of approximately two Appointment Setters, with significant scope for the team to grow as marketing volumes increase.

What We’re Looking For:

We are looking for experienced, commercially minded appointment setters who are comfortable having meaningful conversations about high-value purchases and personal healthcare decisions.

Required Experience

  • Minimum 5 years' experience in appointment setting, inside sales, lead conversion or a similar outbound sales role.

  • Demonstrated experience selling or booking consultations for high-ticket products or services, ideally in the AUD $30,000 to $80,000+ range.

  • Strong experience with a consultative sales and appointment-booking process.

  • Previous experience within medical, dental, healthcare, cosmetic, finance, professional services or another high-consideration industry is highly desirable.

  • Significant experience servicing Australian customers or Australian accounts.

  • Strong understanding of Australian customer expectations, communication styles and business culture.

  • Experience using HubSpot CRM.

  • Proven ability to manage a pipeline of warm leads and maintain disciplined follow-up.

  • Comfortable working within highly structured scripts, processes and performance metrics.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Contact and engage warm inbound leads generated through digital and Meta advertising campaigns.

  • Conduct structured outbound follow-up with prospective patients who have expressed interest in dental implant treatment.

  • Build rapport and understand the patient's circumstances, motivations and treatment objectives.

  • Qualify prospective patients using an established consultative sales framework.

  • Address initial questions and objections professionally while remaining within approved scripts and processes.

  • Book qualified patients into consultations with the appropriate Australian clinic.

  • Maintain consistent follow-up across leads that are not immediately ready to book.

  • Manage lead activity, notes, appointments and pipeline stages accurately within HubSpot.

  • Work closely with Australian clinic and sales teams to maximise attendance and conversion rates.

  • Follow structured scripts, call flows and sales methodologies provided by the client.

  • Participate in ongoing coaching and performance reviews using the client's AI-enabled sales training platform.

  • Support future lead reactivation campaigns and other outbound initiatives as the team develops.

  • Potentially support leads generated through the client's dentist education business as this division grows.

Ready to take your career to the next level? Join us and be part of a team that values your growth, celebrates your achievements, and empowers you to make a real impact.

Apply today and start shaping your future with a company that invests in your success every step of the way!

title: Senior QA/DV Program Manager

You will have the opportunity to work closely with various engineering teams, from HW/SW design, verification, validation and system integration.

Program Management & Execution

QA Program Focus
