Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer is a world-leading global law firm, where our ambition is to help you achieve your goals.

Exceptional client service and the pursuit of excellence are at our core. We invest in and care about our client relationships, which is why so many are longstanding. We enjoy breaking new ground, as we have for over 170 years.

As a fully integrated transatlantic and transpacific firm, we are where you need us to be. Our footprint is extensive and committed across the world’s largest markets, key financial centres and major growth hubs.

At our best tackling complexity and navigating change, we work alongside you on demanding litigation, exacting regulatory work and complex public and private market transactions. We are recognised as leading in these areas.

We are immersed in the sectors and challenges that impact you. We are recognised as standing apart in energy, infrastructure and resources. And we’re focused on areas of growth that affect every business across the world.

All of this is achieved by supporting the growth of our people, who help us deliver on our ambition – which is to help you achieve yours.

Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer: Your goals. Our ambition

The Opportunity

Our internship

Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer Tokyo is offering a limited number of internship opportunities to students who are interested in exploring a future career in the legal industry and gaining first-hand experience in the Japan office of a leading global law firm. The internships are available to both law and non-law students, including postgraduate students.

About the internship

What you can expect

You will work alongside our partners and associates on tasks and projects for our clients, giving you real insight into the depth and breadth of our practice areas. You will also have the opportunity to meet partners, associates and trainees in Tokyo as well as across our global network.

In addition, you may be involved in workshops and presentations and invited to a range of formal and informal social events. By the end of your internship, you should have a clearer sense of whether a future career with an international law firm is right for you, and whether Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer is a place you may wish to pursue that ambition.

Note that our Tokyo office operates as a Gaikokuho Jimu Bengoshi Jimusho (registered foreign law office), and hence we do not practice Japanese law and do not employ Japanese-qualified lawyers. Our lawyers are qualified in jurisdictions outside Japan, and the focus of our offering is cross-border transactions and disputes for Japanese corporate clients.

Eligibility

To be eligible for our Tokyo internship scheme, you must:

  • be a current student or a recent graduate, with study of law preferred but not required;

  • be fluent in English and have a high level of proficiency in Japanese;

  • have the appropriate Japanese visa or other permission required to legally participate in this internship. Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer is unable to assist with, or sponsor, applications to live and work in Japan;

  • have the means to support your own living arrangements and expenses; and

  • be able to commit to a four-week internship in order to maximise the benefits of this scheme.

If you require any adjustments to participate in the internship or application process, please provide the details in your application.

We are looking for self-motivated candidates with strong academic and extracurricular achievements, excellent organisational and communication skills, and a collaborative approach.

During the internship, you will be encouraged to proactively seek opportunities to assist our lawyers and business services teams, including Business Development. You should also ask questions, seek feedback and take opportunities to learn from colleagues. We also encourage you to arrange time to speak with colleagues to learn more about their careers and experiences.

Practice group rotations

Unless agreed otherwise, your internship will be arranged so that you spend time in both the Disputes and Corporate practice groups. As a general rule, each practice group will host one intern at a time.

Our Corporate practice

Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer is a market leader in high-value, complex and multi-jurisdictional corporate non-contentious work. With over 26 years' experience on the ground in Tokyo, our practice focuses on outbound cross-border M&A transactions and strategic investments for Japanese clients around the world. We have invested deeply in cultivating strong, lasting relationships with key market players, including leading Japanese trading houses, industrials and corporates, and other global clients in TMT, manufacturing industrial, healthcare & pharmaceuticals sector.

In addition to our market-leading corporate practice, interns may gain exposure to our Projects, Energy & Infrastructure (PEI) team, which advises on globally significant projects and investments across the energy, power, mining and infrastructure sectors, supporting clients throughout the full project lifecycle. Drawing on our integrated global network, the team provides commercially focused advice on complex cross-border transactions, developments and joint ventures, including those arising from the global energy transition. Our market-leading practice in Japan receives consistent praise and awards, including top-tier rankings in Chambers Asia-Pacific and Asia Pacific Legal 500.

Our Dispute Resolution practice

Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer is a world leader in dispute resolution. We bring international experience and sector knowledge to the resolution of disputes for leading Japanese and international corporations, including trading companies and financial institutions. With over 26 years' experience on the ground in Tokyo, we advise on international arbitration, commercial litigation and other forms of ADR, and are trusted advisers on construction and real estate disputes across the world. We have particular experience in matters arising in the energy and resources, TMT, manufacturing, industrials, healthcare, pharmaceutical, infrastructure and consumer sectors. We also frequently assist our clients with corporate crime and investigations matters. Our market-leading international arbitration practice in Japan is consistently recognised, including through top-tier rankings for Dispute Resolution and Construction in Chambers Asia-Pacific and Asia Pacific Legal 500.

Internship period

The internship scheme has a maximum duration of four weeks. Interns will generally spend two weeks in each of our Disputes and Corporate practice groups. The internship will usually take place between June and August, but timing can be flexible, subject to availability and mutual agreement between the successful candidate(s) and Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer Tokyo.


Application information

Applications for the 2027 internship scheme will be open from 5 October 2026 to 25 October 2026.

If your initial application is successful, you will be contacted for an interview.

We interview on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply early.

What we offer

  • Placement in our market-leading Corporate and Dispute Resolution practice groups for an agreed period, up to a maximum of four weeks in total.

  • Insight into the work of a leading global law firm.

  • A diverse, friendly and engaging working environment.

  • Internships are unpaid in principle; however, paid internships may be offered in exceptional circumstances.

Full time

We are committed to attracting people from all backgrounds and creating a respectful and inclusive culture where everyone thrives. We see this as essential to our success, including our ability to innovate and achieve sustained high performance. This is a key part of our Values—Human, Bold, and Outstanding.

title: Myyjä
description:
Caffitella on vuonna 2008 perustettu Keski-Suomen suurin yksityinen kahvilaketju, jonka sydän sykkii käsin leivotuille herkkuille, aidolle asiakaskohtaamiselle ja mutkattomalle yhteishengelle. Oletko iloinen ja reipas asiakaspalvelija, jolla ei hymy hyydy kiireenkään keskellä? Oletko se tiimipelaaja, joka ottaa vastuuta, kannustaa muita ja toimii oma-aloitteisesti?

  • Iloinen ja asiakaslähtöinen palveluasenne

  • Tiimihenkisyys ja vastuullisuus

  • Kiinnostus myyntiin ja halu kehittyä työssä

  • Joustavuus ja halu onnistua yhdessä.

Etsimme Hervantaan kauppakeskus Duon Caffitellaan henkilöä, joka on aidosti kiinnostunut asiakaspalvelusta ja myynnistä. Toimit sujuvasti yhdessä muiden kanssa ja luot omalta osaltasi lämminhenkistä kahvilakulttuuria.

Mitä odotamme sinulta? -Hygieniapassi -Mahdollisuus työskennellä vaihtelevissa vuoroissa: ma-pe klo 7-20, la-su klo 9-19 välillä. -Aikaisempi kokemus kahvila-, ravintola- tai asiakaspalvelutyöstä on plussaa, muttei välttämätöntä- asenne ratkaisee! -Kiinnostus myynnin tekemiseen ja tavoitteelliseen työskentelyyn -Aktiivinen ja oma-aloitteinen ote. Et pelkää tarttua tehtäviin ja otat vastuuta arjen sujuvuudesta.

Tarjoamme sinulle: -Monipuolisen ja vaihtelevan työn viihtyisässä kahvilamiljöössä -Mukavan ja kannustavan tiimin tuen, meillä et jää yksin -Mahdollisuuden kasvaa ja kehittyä kahvila-alan ammattilaisena -Työpaikan osana kasvavaa ja kotimaista kahvilaketjua.

Jos tunnistit itsesi, lähetä vapaamuotoinen hakemuksesi ja CV:si mahdollisimman pian osoitteeseen laura.liiri-kovanen@caffitella.fi, lisätietoja saat Lauralta numerosta 0504332890. Työpaikka täytetään heti sopivan henkilön löydyttyä. Työ alkaa mahdollisimman pian.

description:
Interested in a career that matters?




Do you want to rethink your impact, and are you passionate about pricing, analytics, and understanding markets?

At Novonesis, we believe biological solutions can help solve some of the world’s biggest challenges. As a Student Assistant in Early Life & Specialized Nutrition (ELSN), you will join the Strategy & Market Expansion team and support our work with pricing, market insights, and business analysis.

This is an opportunity to strengthen your analytical skills and gain practical experience working with commercial data in a global business.


The Role & Your Impact

As a Student Assistant, you will support the ELSN business with a particular focus on pricing analytics, alongside market intelligence and competitor insights.

You will work closely with the Strategy & Market Expansion team to collect, structure, and analyze pricing, market, and commercial data. Through your work, you will help build the fact base used to understand pricing trends, market developments, customer dynamics, and competitor activity.

The role offers hands-on experience with business analysis and exposure to strategic projects and commercial decision-making.


Your Key Responsibilities in This Role

  • Monitor competitors, market developments, and pricing trends within Early Life & Specialized Nutrition.
  • Conduct pricing, market, and commercial analyses to support business decision-making.
  • Build and maintain datasets, dashboards, and analytical tools.
  • Support strategic projects, market assessments, and business cases.
  • Prepare presentations and insights for stakeholders across the organization.

What You’ll Need to Be Successful in This Role

To make the most of the learning opportunities and succeed in the role, you should bring one or more of the following qualities:

  • Strong analytical skills and experience working with Excel.
  • An interest in pricing, commercial analysis, and market dynamics.
  • A structured and detail-oriented approach to working with data.
  • The ability to manage multiple tasks and work independently.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • Preferably at least 1.5 years remaining before completing your studies.

What We Offer

At Novonesis, you will join a collaborative and purpose-driven environment where learning and development are part of everyday work.

You will gain practical experience with analytics, market insights, and commercial decision-making in a global busis.

Working closely with the Early Life & Specialized Nutrition Strategy & Market Expansion team, you will contribute to relevant business analyses while developing your analytical and commercial capabilities.

You will become part of a supportive team focused on collaboration, knowledge sharing, and creating value together.

Ways of Working

The position is based in Hørsholm, Denmark, and is expected to be approximately 10–15 hours per week. The role offers flexibility around exam periods and study commitments.

You should enjoy working in an international environment where priorities can evolve and where project-based work provides opportunities for continuous learning.


Application deadline: 11th of October 2026

title: Communications Systems Technician - Trainee
description:
**** This Position is exclusively for Active Duty and Reserve Military Members actively pursuing the DoD SkillBridge Program ****


Join the MCA Family: Communications Systems Intern Opportunity for Veterans!


Mobile Communications America (MCA), your trusted advisor for wireless communications, data, and security, is seeking a Communications Systems Intern to support our fast-growing Voice team.

(This opportunity is designed specifically for transitioning service members through the DoD SkillBridge Program.)

MCA seeks team members who share our values: Service First, Growth, Teamwork, and Safety. As a Military Friendly Employer, we proudly employ over 250 veterans—and counting. Join us and become part of the MCA family, where we prioritize both work and enjoyment.


Location(s): TUCKER, GA (ATLANTA METRO)


Transferable MOS/AFSCs (Not all-inclusive):

  • 25C, 25L, 25N, 25Q, 25S, 94E, 0621, 0627, 2847, 2841, 1D7X3A, 1C8X3, 1D7X2, 2E1X3, ET, IT, CTM, CTR, CTT


WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING:

  • Supporting RF Engineers and Lead Technicians during system installations, upgrades, and maintenance projects
  • Installing and configuring RF transmission equipment, antennas, repeaters, and 2-way radio systems to manufacturer and company specifications
  • Assisting with RF cabling infrastructure including coax, Cat5/6, and fiber lines for in-building and outdoor communication systems
  • Utilizing RF test equipment, basic hand and power tools for signal alignment, radio programming, and equipment mounting
  • Working across diverse environments such as stadiums, hospitals, schools, and enterprise facilities to deploy and service communication networks
  • Maintaining a clean, organized, and RF-safe workspace compliant with grounding, ESD, and safety standards
  • Delivering reliable, high-quality RF and 2-way radio work that ensures optimal coverage, signal integrity, and customer satisfaction


WHAT YOU WILL BRING TO THE TEAM:

  • 1 year of technical experience or a combination of related education/experience
  • Willingness to learn new technologies and systems
  • Hands-on experience with OEM equipment
  • Ability to read and interpret technical drawings and schematics
  • Flexibility to work various shifts and adapt to evolving technologies
  • Strong communication and professionalism
  • Proven reliability, integrity, and responsibility

WHY VETERANS THRIVE AT MCA:

  • Transferable Skills: Leadership, discipline, and adaptability align with our mission
  • Problem-Solving: Your experience overcoming challenges is invaluable in our dynamic field
  • Camaraderie: Join a team of 250+ veterans who understand your background and values
  • Mission-Driven Culture: We value service and teamwork—just like the military

YOUR ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Work indoors and outdoors in varying conditions
  • Frequent standing, walking, climbing, lifting (up to 50 lbs), and use of tools
  • Occasional ladder use and vehicle operation
  • Use of PPE and ability to handle semi-frequent stressful conditions
  • On-call availability for critical systems maintenance
  • Standard hours: Monday–Friday, with occasional 2nd/3rd shifts and weekends


TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Travel as necessary to support company and customer needs

DIRECT REPORTS:

  • No Direct Reports


WHO WE ARE

Mobile Communications America, Inc. (MCA) provides wireless communication, data, and security solutions that enhance workplace safety, security, and efficiency nationwide. Customers trust us to provide a portfolio of turn-key systems, products, and services — including two-way radio communications, vehicle uplift, security video and access control systems, BDA/DAS, remote monitoring, GPS tracking, SCADA, dispatch, mass notification, and point-to-point wireless networks. Our more than 60,000 customers span industries such as public safety, commercial, manufacturing, education, healthcare, utilities, and government. In addition to being the largest Motorola partner in the U.S., MCA has strategic partnerships with over 1,000 major manufacturers to offer an extensive portfolio of products and technologies.

WHAT WE BELIEVE

We are better together through the MCA Way: living our core values of Service First, Growth, Teamwork, and Safety. We take our work and customers seriously and believe our best work can be fun. A component of our business that embodies the MCA advantage is our “Service First DNA” culture. Service isn’t just a motto for MCA, it’s an integral part of who we are and goes beyond our customers to our employees, partners, shareholders, and communities.

title: Data Center HRP, AWS Builder Experience Team, BeXT AIS
description:
Join Amazon's Builder Experience Team (BeXT) as a Senior Data Center HR Partner and make every day better for the Builders who power AWS. This is a 100% on-site role where you'll serve as the strategic HR partner to cluster operations leadership across multiple clusters. You'll operate with significant autonomy — applying senior judgment in precedent-setting situations, designing scalable mechanisms, and coaching site leadership teams through the most complex people challenges in a rapidly growing business.
What we are looking for:

Adaptability. Manage multiple scenarios across clusters utilizing HR expertise, consulting skills, and influence — often in precedent-setting situations where no clear playbook exists.

High Judgement. Make high-stakes decisions independently in ambiguous, multi-stakeholder situations. Navigate complexity with composure and serve as a go-to advisor for HRPs and site leadership.

Strategic Thinking. Connect sentiment trends, workforce data, and operational signals across clusters to identify systemic patterns. Translate cross-cluster insights into scalable recommendations that shape leadership action.

Influencing. Influence multiple levels of the organization across clusters — from builders to senior site leaders and cross-functional partners — without direct authority. Lead integrated people strategies through partnership.

Coaching. Develop site leadership capability at scale — designing structured coaching approaches and building manager strength across a portfolio of leaders.


Key job responsibilities
Builder Advocacy: Build trust through consistent floor/onsite presence, site walks & gemba walks across multiple clusters. Ensure execution and efficacy of onsite listening mechanisms, identifying and leading strategies based on risk patterns. Foster and role model an environment of inclusion for all Builders, ensuring they feel fully engaged in their work and valued for who they are. Independently manage relationships with employee representative boards.

Strategic Partnership: Serve as the primary HR partner to cluster operations leadership across multiple clusters, developing proactive strategies and goals focused on the Builder experience. Perform cross-cluster systemic risk detection — connecting sentiment trends, workforce data, and operational signals to provide recommendations to site leadership and HRBPs. Coordinate cross-cluster communications in partnership with site leadership. Present at monthly All Manager and All Team Meetings.

HR Expertise: Apply senior judgment to problem-solve across talent management, performance management, compensation, and employee relations — including precedent-setting cases where policy is insufficient or ambiguous. Lead high-complexity employee relations matters, navigating Amazon Policies with senior judgment. Lead workplace investigations in collaboration with Builder Relations and Labor Relations. Drive resolution of systemic pay, internal transfer, and hiring defects in partnership with central teams. Build procedural policy/governance standards (e.g., SOPs) designed for adoption across clusters.

Leadership Development: Design and deliver scalable manager capability programs, coaching site leadership through decision-making with empathy and sound judgment. Identify development opportunities through data, sentiment patterns, and onsite observation. Educate leaders on HR operating model standards and drive adoption across clusters. Support interviews for site manager and technical manager roles.

Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with HRBPs, Centers of Excellence (COEs), Employee Relations, and Labor Relations to deliver integrated people strategies across multiple clusters. Partner with New Hire Experience teams on orientation, onboarding, and lifecycle support for new site launches. Mentor HRPs and drive peer enablement. Manage through ambiguity in a fast-paced, continuously innovating environment.

Role Requirements

This is a 100% Onsite role and requires the ability to travel to assigned Data Center sites across multiple clusters within a region (estimated 30–40% travel).

Data Center environments are 24/7 operational facilities; flexibility to support off-shift populations and respond to time-sensitive people matters is expected.

This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports; leadership is demonstrated through influence, mentorship, and cross-functional partnership.



A day in the life
You'll conduct site walks across clusters with Operations, Safety, and Deployment leadership — staying close to what's happening on the ground while maintaining the altitude to spot patterns across sites. You'll analyze sentiment data and roundtable feedback to detect systemic risk, then partner with cluster leadership to translate those patterns into action. You'll coach site leaders through complex, high-stakes people decisions, lead workplace investigations, and design mechanisms and SOPs that drive consistency across your portfolio. You'll mentor HRPs, coordinate with cross-functional partners on integrated people strategies, and manage employee representative board relationships independently.

Job Description Summary:

This is administrative and clerical work in support of an instructional unit with one instructional program, or a small group of closely associated programs, at times of a confidential and sensitive nature. An incumbent in this job is primarily responsible for coordinating the non-academic administrative functions and performing support tasks for one instructional program, or a small group of closely associated programs. Duties include providing customer service to students, orienting faculty to administrative tasks, preparing and processing budgets, faculty workloads and timetables; processing student applications and block registrations; and assisting with promotional and informational activities. An incumbent receives direction from a Program Coordinator and reports to a Dean.

Job Description:

ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLES OF DUTIES

  • Prepares and enters or submits section plans, timetables, faculty workloads, faculty PD proposals and reports, and faculty sick leave reports according to the Coordinator’s manual, and in consultation with and for the approval of the Coordinator. Contacts the Registrar’s Office and Administrative Analysts to investigate and resolve problems.
  • Prepares operating budgets and capital requests in consultation with and for the approval of the Coordinator. Tracks, monitors and reconciles cost centers including depositing and recording revenue, processing disbursements and charge backs, printing and reviewing management reports, and contacting Financial Services as required. Resolves discrepancies or brings them to the attention of the Coordinator. Has signing authority within University guidelines. Maintains petty cash fund.
  • Ensures that appropriate funds are collected from students including preparing and submitting exceptional tuition fee requests, collecting and tracking tuition fee deposits, contacting sponsors to ensure that sponsored fees are collected by Financial Services, and collecting fees for conferences and student retreats. Processes refunds as required.
  • Facilitates communication and arrangements between the university and potential students, current students, alumni and faculty. Assists in the recruitment of students and the promotion of programs. This includes answering enquiries; referring people to other campus services; preparing calendar and brochure information; uploading information to a web page; drafting and/or revising student handbooks and manuals; coordinating mailings; and maintaining and monitoring an electronic bulletin board system. This may also include the administration of any social media channels that the department may have.
  • Processes student applications and application materials, including portfolios. Screens for completeness of material. Arranges student interviews and portfolio reviews. Block registers students.
  • Prepares program profiles and new course proposals under the direction of the Coordinator.
  • Compiles faculty evaluations as instructed by the Dean’s Office and according to the CCFA collective agreement including visiting classrooms to administer student evaluations, collecting other evaluations, and tabulating and preparing material for review by the evaluation committee. This is a sensitive and confidential process.
  • Distributes, collects, checks and submits grade sheets.
  • Orients new Coordinators to administrative tasks, guidelines and deadlines as outlined in the Coordinator’s Manual. Orients new faculty to University administrative guidelines.
  • Ascertains requirements for material and equipment for resale to students and places orders.
  • Arranges and attends department meetings, including preparing agendas and taking minutes. Serves on university committees as required.
  • Invigilates extra-sessional exams for one student or a small number of students, or arranges for testing or invigilation.
  • Prepares postings and arranges interviews for faculty hires.
  • Plans and organizes local special events and makes travel arrangements.
  • Organizes departmental elections.
  • Assists faculty and staff with the operation of computers, phones, faxes and other office equipment.
  • Coordinates office allocations and moves.
  • Performs support duties including drafting correspondence; ordering supplies, equipment and duplicating; contacting facilities for maintenance and office moves; maintaining departmental files, lists and other records, including databases; opening and distributing mail; and coordinating lab, locker or flat file access.
  • May be required to take training and act in the capacity of a floor warden as part of the University’s Emergency Preparedness Plan (Fire, W.H.M.I.S., and Earthquake).
  • Performs duties related to the qualifications and requirements of the position.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, ABILITIES AND SKILLS

  • Thorough knowledge of the regulations, policies and procedures governing the program.
  • Thorough knowledge of the Coordinator’s Manual and University policy and procedure governing faculty workload, admissions, registration and financial services.
  • Thorough knowledge of word processing applications.
  • Considerable knowledge of program content and flow.
  • Considerable knowledge of business English and spelling.
  • Considerable knowledge of office practices and equipment, bookkeeping and arithmetic.
  • Considerable knowledge of spreadsheet and database applications.
  • For specified programs: considerable knowledge of web posting and bulletin board applications.
  • Considerable knowledge of the CCFA Collective Agreement articles pertaining to regularization, instructional and lab supervisor workloads, forward averaging, and overload/underload.
  • Ability to multitask, apply organization skills to meet deadlines, and work with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to understand and follow complex oral and written instructions, and communicate information effectively, both orally and in writing.
  • Ability to adapt to changing situations.
  • Ability to maintain attention to detail with constant interruption.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with a diverse group of other employees, students and the general public
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive issues with tact and diplomacy.
  • Ability to establish and maintain administrative procedures.
  • Skill in keyboarding to 50 wpm.

REQUIRED TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE

  • Completion of two years (approximately 60 credits) of post-secondary business education comparable to the Diploma in Business Administration program offered at Capilano University.
  • Two years of directly related administrative support experience, including experience in an educational setting with significant student contact.

title: Culinary Assistant
description:
At Holy Cross, we are focused on creating a world-class workforce by attracting and retaining employees dedicated to fostering a culture of professionalism, pride, mutual trust, and respect—one that values appreciation and recognition, empowering each of us to flourish both individually and collectively. We seek candidates who are inspired by our mission and values, and who are eager to make a meaningful difference on our campus. Learn more about Life at Holy Cross here.

At Holy Cross Dining, you are part of more than a food-service operation—you are an essential part of the student experience and the broader College community. Our culinary team plays an important role in creating a welcoming, connected, and enjoyable campus experience by providing high-quality meals and exceptional service to students, faculty, staff, and guests.
As a Culinary Assistant, you will contribute to an environment where every meal and interaction is an opportunity to make someone feel welcomed, valued, and connected to the Holy Cross community. You will help prepare and serve quality food while supporting a positive dining experience through hospitality, teamwork, inclusion, and service.
We are looking for team members who take pride in their work, enjoy working collaboratively, and understand that great hospitality extends beyond the food—it is about the experience we create for every member of our community.

Job Description

DAYS & HOURS:

Holy Cross Dining staff are considered Emergency Essential Personnel and are required to report to work during times of inclement weather. Flexibility is required, and schedules may change based on departmental needs, the academic calendar, campus events, and operational requirements.


CURRENT SCHEDULE: Sunday - Thursday / 12:00 PM – 8:30 PM


Perform a variety of duties to support the preparation and service of meals for students, guests, and members of the College community, following established practices, methods, and food safety standards. Responsibilities include serving guests, assisting with food production, stocking and rotating products, and setting up, maintaining, and cleaning food production and service areas in accordance with established sanitation standards.

This position contributes to a welcoming and positive dining experience by providing quality food and exceptional service to students and guests. Responsibilities also include safely operating a variety of food service equipment, including slicing machines, grills, fryolators, pizza ovens, stir-fry equipment, and similar tools.


MAJOR AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY FOR THIS POSITION

  • Prepare and cook food items to order, ensuring adherence to established standards and specifications.
  • Follow menu and recipe guidelines precisely to maintain consistency and quality across all food items.
  • Ensure all menu items are consistently prepared, properly portioned, of the highest quality, and served at the correct temperatures. Accurately complete temperature log book charts.
  • Maintain a clean, safe, organized, and fully functional work area that is adequately stocked and properly rotated at all times.
  • Safely and effectively operate food service equipment, including slicing machines, grills, fryolators, pizza ovens, stir-fry equipment, and similar equipment.
  • Supervise on-call staff, student captains/workers, and temporary employees, providing direction and support on routine tasks to ensure smooth and efficient operations.
  • Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability by working in various areas of the servery and dining operation as assigned by management.
  • Provide exceptional customer service by serving guests in a friendly, professional, attentive, and welcoming manner.
  • Contribute to a positive dining experience for students, guests, and members of the College community through quality food, hospitality, and responsive service.
  • Assist with the setup, service, and cleanup of catered events, ensuring all operational and service standards are met.
  • Accurately complete service records and inventory data within the FoodPro system to ensure proper tracking and reporting.
  • Demonstrate proficiency in accommodating students with special dietary restrictions, ensuring their needs are met with care and in accordance with established food safety protocols. Seek guidance from management when questions arise.
  • Understand and apply food waste management practices, utilizing FIFO (First In, First Out) to minimize waste and maintain inventory efficiency.
  • Adhere to all state and local food safety regulations, sanitation standards, and departmental procedures to ensure compliance and uphold the highest standards of food safety.
  • Perform other similar or related duties as required or requested.

RESPONSIBILITIES OF ALL HOSPITALITY EMPLOYEES

  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately and in a timely manner.
  • Follow all chemical handling and safety guidelines according to applicable Safety Data Sheets (SDS).
  • Provide superior customer service and demonstrate strong communication skills to create a welcoming, friendly, and professional environment for all guests.
  • Offer training and support to co-workers, staff, and students where applicable.
  • Follow all verbal and written instructions from managers and supervisors.
  • Have the ability to frequently lift up to 25 pounds, occasionally lift up to 50 pounds, and lift up to 100 pounds with assistance.
  • All staff are considered Emergency Essential Personnel and are required to report to work during times of inclement weather.
  • Maintain schedule flexibility and remain aware of the academic calendar and special event dates. Schedules may be adjusted based on campus events and operational needs.
  • Demonstrate innovation and initiative in performing the responsibilities of the position.
  • Be comfortable sharing suggestions and ideas that support process improvements, operational efficiency, and an enhanced dining experience.
  • Comply with all safety and risk management practices, policies, and procedures.
  • Demonstrate the ability to succeed in a fast-paced and high-pressure environment while maintaining professionalism and attention to detail.
  • Communicate with guests, co-workers, and other members of the College community with professionalism and respect.
  • Demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to the department’s core values in daily work and interactions.
  • Adhere to the uniform standards applicable to the position.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS FOR THIS POSITION

  • Up to two years of related work experience is preferred.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
  • Ability to frequently lift up to 25 pounds, occasionally lift up to 50 pounds, and lift up to 100 pounds with assistance.
  • ServSafe Food Safety Certification or training is required. If training or certification is not current, it must be completed within 3–6 months of the date of hire.
  • Food allergy training is essential. Prior experience preparing meals for individuals with food allergies or special dietary restrictions is preferred. Candidates without prior experience must complete the required training upon hire. Initial training will include a review of relevant information, departmental responsibilities, and the Food Allergy Program.
  • Excellent customer service and communication skills are required to provide a welcoming, professional, and safe environment for students and guests.
  • Upon hire, the following additional training must be completed annually: Title IX Harassment Training and Security Awareness Training.

CORE COMPETENCIES

  • Inclusion: Actively engaging with the values of the College by promoting a work environment that embraces diversity and demonstrating respect for the opinions and beliefs of others.
  • Innovation: Performing one’s job with creativity and proactivity, improving procedures and problem-solving.
  • Mission/Service Orientation: Focusing on service to others and contributing to the College’s collective mission.
  • Responsibility: Taking ownership of one’s actions and accountability for one’s tasks and duties.
  • Collaboration: Exchanging information, ideas, and thoughts with others in a manner that is proactive and enhances partnerships.

DISCLAIMER

The description above represents the most significant duties of this position but does not exclude other occasional work assignments not mentioned, the inclusion of which would be in conformity with the factor degrees assigned.

title: Supervisor, Security Specialist
description:
Why USAA?

At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.

The Opportunity

As a dedicated Supervisor, Security Specialist you will be responsible for monitoring the safety and security of employees, contractors, visitors and facilities worldwide. Able to use but oversees shifter personnel to utilize a variety of tools ranging from access control, video management, computer aided dispatch, alarm monitoring, report management, intelligence sources, radio dispatch consoles, and in-house tools. The Security Operations Center detects, analyzes, and dispatches security officers, monitors incidents, and provides support. Additionally, we notify appropriate strategic partners, and/or external responding agencies regarding any adverse conditions impacting the association or its employees, contractors, and visitors. These incidents may range from simple theft to active assailant. Works under minimal supervision and leads shift operations. Performs complex work assignments and problem resolution across multiple disciplines. Collaborates with all levels of USAA management and internal partners to assess business or personnel issues related to security, safety, and risk. Provides training, coaching, feedback, and performance management for Security Specialists on shift.

We offer a flexible work environment that requires an individual to be in the office 5 days per week. This position can be based in one of the following locations: San Antonio, TX ; Phoenix, AZ. Relocation assistance is not available for this position.

What you'll do:

  • Oversees and leads association wide security activities for each shift of the 24x7x365 Security Operations Center.
  • Conducts ongoing review of multiple systems and sources to detect potential risks.
  • Inspects alarm cause and impact and creates recommendation reports.
  • Provides supervision for major incidents.
  • Gathers information, analyzes data trends, identifies root cause(s), and proactive provides information to leadership and appropriate stakeholders.
  • Leverages internal and external partnerships to proactively solve business problems and ensure appropriate elements are communicated in a clear and timely manner.
  • Supervise shift personnel to ensure procedural requirements are met.
  • Responsible for the leadership, performance management, and development of specialists.
  • Manage formal supervisory duties, including recommendations for personnel actions, performance evaluations, timekeeping, and Personal Time Off (PTO) requests.
  • Guides team members in the development and delivery of their work product.
  • Build and manage a team through development, retention, coaching, performance management, and other managerial activities for the assigned shift.
  • Ensures risks associated with business activities are effectively identified, measured, monitored, and controlled in accordance with risk and compliance policies and procedures.


Experiences that will support your success:

  • Bachelor's degree; OR 4 years of relevant education and/or experience.
  • 4 or more years of operational experience in a Security Operations Center, Public Safety Answering Point, or Law Enforcement Dispatch Center environment.
  • Proficiency in operating and managing CCTV systems, access control systems, and alarm monitoring systems. Ability to learn new systems quickly.
  • Proficient level of business acumen in the areas of the business operations, industry practices and emerging trends required.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with law enforcement, emergency responders, and senior security stakeholders, including leading coordination during critical incidents.

What sets you apart:

  • Previous people leader experience in an operation center.
  • Previous experience managing emergency incidents.
  • Previous experience using CCure, Victor VMS, AVTEC, Perspective.
  • US military experience through military service or a military spouse/domestic partner [optional]

Compensation range: The salary range for this position is: $63,590.00- $114,450.00.

    Compensation: USAA has an effective process for assessing market data and establishing ranges to ensure we remain competitive. You are paid within the salary range based on your experience and market data of the position. The actual salary for this role may vary by location.

    Employees may be eligible for pay incentives based on overall corporate and individual performance and at the discretion of the USAA Board of Directors.

    The above description reflects the details considered necessary to describe the principal functions of the job and should not be construed as a detailed description of all the work requirements that may be performed in the job.

    Benefits: At USAA our employees enjoy best-in-class benefits to support their physical, financial, and emotional wellness. These benefits include comprehensive medical, dental and vision plans, 401(k), pension, life insurance, parental benefits, adoption assistance, paid time off program with paid holidays plus 16 paid volunteer hours, and various wellness programs. Additionally, our career path planning and continuing education assists employees with their professional goals.

    For more details on our outstanding benefits, visit our benefits page on USAAjobs.com.

title: DevOps Engineer
description:
What we’re all about.

It isn’t often you get to be part of a tech company that, since 2016, has been innovating the data analytics market in ways no-one else can. Our technology started out in FinTech, helping tackle serious criminal activity. Now, its potential is virtually limitless. Working at the company isn't just intellectually stimulating. We’re a real team. Collaborating and constantly engineering better and better solutions. We’re ambitious, we think things through and we’re on a mission to discover just how far we can go. Nearly half of our colleagues come from an ethnic or religious minority background. We’re made up of people from 47 nationalities who speak over 20 languages. As a diverse mix of individuals, we make one big unstoppable team.

If our incredible culture sounds like you, we’d love you to join us.

What will you be doing?

You’ll be joining one of our DevOps teams in our R&D department working on the the company Cloud Platform and accompanying solutions. The platform is comprised of a landscape of low maintenance, on-demand, and highly secure environments. Our environments host our software for our customers and partners to use, they also service a variety of internal use cases including underpinning the work of our R&D teams to develop the company Platform software.

You’ll be heavily involved with our cloud-based technical infrastructure, with responsibilities surrounding improving the availability and resilience of our platform, improving its usability and security, ensuring we stay at the forefront of technical innovation, and reducing toil across our estate.

You will also work alongside our software engineering teams to leverage DevOps techniques to support our software release activities and work on unique cloud-based product offerings for our customers to use in their own DevOps processes on their own Cloud estate.

Our tech stack

  • A strong focus on Docker/Kubernetes/Istio
  • DevOps tooling/automation written with Bash/Python/Groovy/Jenkins/Golang
  • Provisioning software/frameworks (Elasticsearch/Spark/Hadoop/PostgreSQL)
  • Infrastructure Management - CasC, IasC (Ansible, Terraform, Packer)
  • Log and metric aggregation with Fluentd, Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager
  • Public Cloud, primarily GCP, but also AWS and Azure

Requirements

What do I need to have?

  • Take pride in designing, building and delivering high quality well engineered solutions to complex problems
  • Take a big picture approach to solving problems, taking care to ensure that the solution works well within the wider system
  • In-depth exposure to a handful of the key parts of our tech stack listed above
  • Experience with programming/scripting/automation
  • Good appreciation for information security principals
  • Experience with infrastructure management and general Linux administration

Experience in the following would be beneficial:

  • Experience managing microservice based architectures (scaling, upgrading, traffic management, deployment strategies)
  • Experience mentoring junior engineers
  • Experience with software build and release engineering

Our mission.

We have one mission. To help businesses grow. To make data easier. And to make the world a better place. We’re not a start-up. Not anymore. But we’ve not been around that long either. What we are is a collection of bright, passionate minds harnessing complexities and helping our clients and their communities. One culture, made of many. Heading in one direction – the future.

It’s all about you.

We want you to feel welcome, valued, and respected - because it’s your individuality and passion that make you Q. We see that, and we celebrate it. That’s why we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse work environment, continuously improving to ensure everyone belongs. Our recruitment process is designed to be inclusive and accessible. If you need any reasonable adjustments or accommodations, please let our Talent Acquisition Team know - we’re happy to assist.

No matter your race, beliefs, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, neurodiversity, or abilities—whoever you are—if you're a passionate, curious, and caring human eager to push the boundaries of what’s possible, we want to hear from you.

title: Intern, Specialized Transportation Services
description:
Job Description

College Intern – Specialized Transportation Services (Vanpool Program)

Under direct supervision, this internship provides the opportunity to strengthen your problem-solving, communication, collaboration, and decision-making skills while gaining firsthand exposure to the important role vanpool services play within OCTA and the community. You’ll work alongside transportation professionals and contribute to projects that directly support Vanpool operations, program efficiency, and mobility throughout Orange County. You will participate in a variety of projects and gain practical experience in a professional environment that encourages leadership, teamwork, and creative problem solving. As part of the Intern program, you will be exposed to OCTA's career opportunities in the transportation industry. You will gain deeper awareness of transportation's many facets through your OCTA orientation, projects and teams, and internal networking.

OCTA's College Intern Program is a year-round paid student/intern program. You will gain real world work experience on meaningful projects under the guidance of a transportation professional. You will have the opportunity to use problem solving, communication and decision-making skills as you gain valuable work experience. You will also work with a mentor and benefit from career counseling.

The pay range is from $20.00 - $23.00 per hour depending on your education level. This position is not eligible for employee benefits. The work schedule will consist of approximately 20 hours a week, not to exceed 1,000 hours within a continuous 12-month period. This is a part-time, year-round college internship position.

This posting will remain open until a candidate is selected.

What You’ll Do

  • Support the day-to-day activities and initiatives of OCTA’s Vanpool Program
  • Assist with projects designed to improve vanpool operations, program efficiency, and customer service
  • Support the collection, organization, and analysis of information related to Vanpool program activities
  • Assist with preparing reports, spreadsheets, presentations, correspondence, and other program materials
  • Participate in program-related projects and activities that support transportation and mobility needs throughout Orange County
  • Collaborate with OCTA staff and other partners to support program goals and initiatives
  • Apply creative problem-solving skills to real-world transportation and operational challenges
  • Participate in meetings, projects, and other learning opportunities that provide exposure to OCTA’s transportation programs and business operations
  • Take on progressively responsible assignments while developing professional, analytical, communication, and organizational skills

What We’re Looking For

  • Currently enrolled full-time college student (Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, or Senior) at an accredited two- or four-year college or university.
  • A student interested in gaining professional experience in transportation, business, public administration, operations, planning, or related field
  • Minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 or higher.
  • Interest in public transportation, shared mobility, vanpooling, or transportation program operations
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a team-oriented professional environment
  • Strong problem-solving skills with an interest in developing creative solutions
  • Ability to manage assignments, meet deadlines, and adapt to changing priorities
  • Initiative, professionalism, and a willingness to learn
  • Ability to perform entry-level professional work and develop increasingly complex knowledge and skills

Why You’ll Love It Here

  • Gain hands-on experience supporting a transportation program that provides mobility options throughout Orange County
  • Contribute to projects that can have a direct impact on vanpool operations and program efficiency
  • Learn how transportation programs are developed, administered, and delivered in a public agency environment
  • Work alongside experienced transportation professionals and build valuable professional relationships
  • Strengthen your leadership, collaboration, communication, and creative problem-solving skills
  • Gain exposure to OCTA’s broader operations and explore potential career opportunities in the transportation industry

Join a team where innovation, integrity, and strategic thinking are valued.
Apply now to gain meaningful professional experience and help support OCTA’s Vanpool Program and mobility options throughout Orange County.

title: Software Factory Engineer IV
description:
Start Date: Immediate
JHNA, CTSi, and EXPANSIA have come together to form a Defense Technology platform named Aether Aerospace focused on delivering high-impact technologies, technology-enabled services and advanced manufacturing solutions to the U.S. Department of Defense and related national security customers. Backed by Falfurrias Management Partners, the platform brings together deep domain expertise across Army, Navy, and Air Force and Space Force programs, digital engineering, systems integration, and specialized manufacturing capabilities.

The combined organization operates as a multi-entity aerospace and defense technology and tech-enabled services and manufacturing enterprise positioned for scalable growth, operational excellence, and long-term value creation

OVERVIEW
Full-time/Permanent Employee
Location: Remote
As a Software Factory Engineer IV, you will design, integrate, and improve secure software factory capabilities used by multiple mission software teams. You will connect cloud infrastructure, DevSecOps pipelines, development tools, cybersecurity controls, observability, and reusable platform services into a coherent delivery environment. You will advise programs on how to onboard to and use existing Department of the Air Force software factories, such as Platform One, ODIN, and DAF CloudWorks, including the technical, security, governance, and operational steps that follow initial access. Working as an emerging technical authority with considerable latitude, you will guide complex integration decisions, improve common patterns and developer experience, and partner with government and contractor stakeholders to deliver reliable, accreditable software.

RESPONSIBILTIES

  • Design and integrate software factory services spanning source control, CI/CD, artifact repositories, registries, security scanning, test automation, secrets, cloud infrastructure, and observability

  • Advise programs on factory selection and onboarding, including application architecture, access and identity, environment needs, interfaces, inherited and application-specific controls, release paths, and sustainment responsibilities

  • Lead technical integration of applications with established factories, including Platform One, ODIN, or DAF CloudWorks as applicable; resolve gaps between factory services and program delivery needs

  • Establish reusable CI/CD templates, infrastructure-as-code modules, container baselines, deployment patterns, and platform services that scale across application teams

  • Architect secure cloud and container environments, including networking, identity, secrets, storage, compute, Kubernetes, logging, and separation of environments

  • Embed automated testing, SAST/DAST/SCA, SBOMs, artifact provenance, vulnerability management, and evidence collection into delivery workflows in partnership with RMF/ATO stakeholders

  • Define application onboarding and self-service practices, documentation, templates, APIs, and support pathways that improve developer experience and reduce time to first deployment

  • Guide artifact promotion, configuration management, deployment, monitoring, incident response, and reliability practices across development, test, and production

  • Troubleshoot complex platform and toolchain issues, assess design tradeoffs, and implement changes that improve security, availability, performance, and maintainability

  • Mentor engineers and application teams, share architectural patterns and lessons learned, and coordinate technical decisions with customer and cybersecurity stakeholders

  • Measure platform adoption, onboarding friction, delivery performance, and operational health; use the results to prioritize improvements

  • Provide technical support to operational strategies aligned within your program and initiatives that optimize processes, enhance productivity, and ensure quality across all program functions

  • Ensure 100% of planned hours are worked and recorded

  • Identify and forward to your leadership any opportunities that could lead to growth within your work area

  • Participate in growth efforts as requested

  • Ensure all contractual deliverables are met/exceeded to the customer's satisfaction

  • Complete personal PDP and attend Staff Meeting and Storytime (with camera on)

  • Within your program, build productive and positive professional relationships with clients

  • Execute all contract requirements as assigned in accordance with the contract-specific LCAT and requirements

  • Perform other related duties as assigned

KEY QUALIFICATIONS

Clearance: Active TS/SCI
Education and Years of Experience: Bachelor's (or equivalent) with 8 - 10 years of experience, or a Master's with 6 - 8 years of experience in software factory engineering, DevSecOps, cloud/platform engineering, or IT operations

  • Extensive experience designing and integrating shared software delivery platforms, DevSecOps toolchains, and reusable CI/CD patterns across teams

  • Demonstrated experience guiding application teams through onboarding and sustained use of an established software factory, including security, access, integration, and release considerations

  • Proficiency in infrastructure as code such as Terraform, Ansible, or CloudFormation and advanced scripting with Python, Bash, or PowerShell

  • Strong cloud architecture expertise in AWS or Azure, including identity, networking, storage, compute, containers, and Kubernetes

  • Hands-on knowledge of automated security controls, software supply-chain protections, observability, and RMF/ATO evidence needs in DoD delivery

PREFERRED ADDITIONAL QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with Platform One, ODIN, DAF CloudWorks, or a comparable DoD software factory from both the platform and program application perspectives

  • Experience establishing standardized onboarding, self-service platform capabilities, and reusable development patterns for multiple programs

  • Knowledge of hardened container baselines, SBOMs, artifact provenance, security scanning, and continuous assessment practices

  • Experience with high-availability cloud architecture, networking, monitoring, and incident response

  • Experience mentoring engineers and evaluating AI-assisted or agentic development workflows, including MCP integrations, in a controlled delivery environment

title: Electromechanical Technician I, II or III - Evenings
description:
2551 Valmont Dr Brenham Texas 77833-5418

Why Valmont

We’re Here to Move the World Forward.

Valmont impacts millions of people around the world every day, yet they might not realize the many ways. Our technology is helping feed the growing population, supplying the world with more reliable energy and access to renewables, enhancing connectivity in remote and urban locations to create a sustainable future and so much more. Simply put, Valmont is advancing agricultural productivity and reimagining vital infrastructure to make life better.

Join a Fortune 1000 company that respects hard work, honors diversity and invests in our employees as we focus on creating the world of tomorrow, today. We are the modern workforce. Are you ready to move the world forward? Apply now.

We are hiring Electromechanical Technicians with a strong focus on industrial electrical maintenance and troubleshooting.


In this hands-on role, you will diagnose, maintain, and repair electrical and electromechanical systems that support manufacturing operations. You'll work with motors, controls, industrial electrical components, power distribution, and equipment up to 480V, along with mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems.

Evening Shift | 2nd Shift Standard Schedule:

Monday–Friday, 3:00 PM–11:00 PM*

*Additional hours outside the standard shift schedule may be required based on business needs.

📈 Built-In Pay Progression: Increase opportunities at 90 days, 1 year, and 2 years

💵 Shift Differential: Additional $1.00/hour for off-shift positions

📊 Periodic Wage Review Opportunities

🎯 Annual Discretionary Bonus Opportunity

Candidates may be hired at the Technician I, II, or III level based on electrical experience, technical proficiency, education, and overall industrial maintenance background.

What You'll Do

  • Troubleshoot and repair industrial electrical and electromechanical systems
  • Diagnose electrical faults using meters and other testing equipment
  • Maintain and repair motors, controls, relays, contactors, disconnects, transformers, sensors, and related components
  • Install and service electrical equipment and components, including systems up to 480V, based on qualifications and position level
  • Read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and equipment prints
  • Troubleshoot production equipment to identify electrical and mechanical causes of downtime
  • Perform preventive and corrective maintenance
  • Troubleshoot mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems as needed
  • Follow lockout/tagout and established electrical safety procedures
  • Document repairs and communicate equipment and safety concerns

Find the Level That Fits Your Experience

Position level will be determined based on the selected candidate's electrical experience, technical skills, education, industrial maintenance experience, and ability to meet the qualifications of the applicable technician level.

Electromechanical Technician I* | LG11 ($28.72 - $29.95)

*Developing Electrical & Maintenance Technician

  • 1+ year of industrial equipment maintenance experience
  • Experience using electrical diagnostic and testing equipment
  • Working knowledge of industrial electrical systems and components
  • Ability to read basic electrical schematics and equipment prints
  • Foundational mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic troubleshooting skills
  • Performs routine electrical and equipment repairs while developing more advanced troubleshooting capabilities
  • High school diploma or GED required

Electromechanical Technician II* | LG13 ($32.56 - $33.95)

*Experienced Electrical & Maintenance Technician

  • Generally, 2 to 3 years of relevant industrial maintenance experience
  • Strong electrical troubleshooting and diagnostic skills
  • Experience with motors, relays, contactors, disconnects, transformers, sensors, motor starters, and control components
  • Ability to troubleshoot and repair industrial electrical equipment with limited instruction
  • Experience with electrical installations and equipment up to 480V
  • Ability to read and troubleshoot from electrical schematics and wiring diagrams
  • Solid mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic troubleshooting capabilities
  • Technical school or apprenticeship training preferred

Electromechanical Technician III* | LG15 ($37.94 - $38.63)

*Advanced Electrical & Controls Technician

  • Advanced industrial electrical and electromechanical troubleshooting experience
  • Ability to independently diagnose complex electrical and equipment failures
  • Strong working knowledge of PLCs, machine controls, motors, control circuits, and power distribution
  • Experience installing, maintaining, modifying, and troubleshooting industrial control equipment
  • Experience working with electrical equipment and systems up to 480V
  • Advanced ability to interpret electrical schematics and use diagnostic equipment
  • Strong mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic troubleshooting capabilities
  • Serves as a technical resource to other maintenance team members
  • Electromechanical or Electrical Technology degree preferred

What We're Looking For

We're especially interested in candidates with hands-on experience in:

Industrial Electrical Troubleshooting • 480V Systems • Motors & Motor Controls • Electrical Schematics • PLCs & Controls • Relays & Contactors • Power Distribution • Preventive Maintenance • Manufacturing Equipment

Successful candidates should also:

  • Put safety first
  • Enjoy hands-on electrical troubleshooting and problem-solving
  • Work effectively independently and as part of a team
  • Be comfortable working in an industrial manufacturing environment
  • Be able to perform the physical requirements of the position
  • Be available for overtime based on business needs

Grow With Us

Our Electromechanical Technician structure provides a progressive technical career path. Employees can advance as they expand their electrical knowledge, troubleshooting capabilities, training, experience, and overall technical proficiency.

Working Environment and Physical Efforts:

Most of this job is performed in an indoor shop environment. The temperature range can be from 100 degrees in the summer to about 50 degrees in the winter. Most operations may expose employee to some type of disagreeable working conditions (wind, cold, heat, dust, dirt, fumes, noise, vibration, water, or oil). Working conditions may vary with specific work assignments. Some areas of the plant can be a noisy at times with sound levels reaching above 85 decibels. Hearing protection is available for those areas. Safety glasses and metatarsal safety shoes are required at all times in the plant. Gloves are required during certain operations. Face shield is required in addition to safety glasses when grinding. The employee will operate machines that use liquid coolant and may also be exposed to cast iron dust. The employees must be able to spend the entire work shift on their feet within the plant environment. Some outdoor work is required which includes work in conditions with abnormal temperatures. Employee works around material stacked overhead height. Conditions range from clean work to exposure to odors, fumes, drafts, wet conditions, dirt, grease, smoke, dust, noise, high temperatures and low frigid temperatures. These conditions range from severe to mild and can happen daily and in any combination. An Electromechanical Technician works in disagreeable weather conditions nearly 30% of the year.

Employee must stand and walk, as well as handle parts, tools and equipment, gripping and grasping, on a frequent to constant basis. On an occasional to frequent basis, operator is required to lift/carry parts. Most weight moved is less than 30 lb. Although a few items do weigh more, a maximum lift of 50 lb. is all that is required. Standing, bending, pivoting, walking and reaching overhead are required during most of the shift. Climbing ladders, pulling wire through conduit, hanging fixtures and electrical components also requires a physical exertion. Lifting, carrying, bending, kneeling, stretching, crawling and working in awkward and/or confined positions is frequent with any electromechanical technician. Some of the physical tasks include hanging gearboxes on top of machines, changing brakes or the motors on cranes.

Mental and Visual Effort

The functions of this job require the employee to be alert at all times. Working in a fast-paced environment as well as the repetitious nature of this job requires both mental and visual concentration. The technician must be able to work quickly to repair plant equipment so operations can resume. There are often high stress situations where the technician needs to be able to work under adverse conditions for long periods of time using intense mental and visual concentration. Good hand to eye coordination with a good sense of depth perception is required at all time. Technicians need to be able to distinguish colors and be capable of reading manuals, schematics, labels, and other printed materials. Adequate hearing is required to diagnose problems with machines and equipment. Mental and visual concentration is needed to prevent injury to oneself, fellow workers and/or damage to the product. The use of any equipment or tools requires the employee to be alert at all times. If employee does not have a valid license from either of these states, the determination of acceptable vision will be made by the Safety Department on an individual basis.

Benefits

Valmont offers employees and their families a comprehensive Total Wellbeing benefit package to ensure their individual and family’s overall wellness needs are met. Some offerings are dependent upon the role, work schedule, or location and can include the following:

  • Healthcare (medical, prescription drugs, dental and vision)

  • 401k retirement plan with company match

  • Paid time off

  • Employer paid life insurance

  • Employer paid short-term and long-term disability including maternity leave

  • Work Life Support

  • Tuition Reimbursement up to $5,250 per year

  • Voluntary programs like tobacco cessation, Type 2 diabetes reversal, one-on-one health coaching, mortgage services and more

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Santander () is evolving from a global, high-impact brand into a technology-driven organisation, and our people are at the heart of this journey. Together, we are driving a customer-centric transformation that values bold thinking, innovation, and the courage to challenge what’s possible.

THE DIFFERENCE YOU MAKE


Santander is looking for a Customer Experience Advisor based out of Darlington Branch , working 35 hours per week, on a rota’d basis Monday to Saturday, between 8am & 6pm.

What’s not in doubt is that you’ll have plenty of support. Life in a branch can be busy, varied and challenging, so we’re a close-knit team.


You’ll be totally flexible in your approach and comfortable in undertaking a broad range of activities. This means not limiting your time and focus on one particular element of your role. You’ll thrive on the variety this gives you and take satisfaction for operating in a multi-skilled environment. You’re the eyes and ears of our business after all.


We’re shaping the way we work through innovation, cutting-edge technology, collaboration and the freedom to explore new ideas. To succeed in this role, you will be responsible for:

The Event Technology & Security role is responsible for planning, deploying, operating, and continuously improving technology solutions that support the security and safety of corporate events. title: Customer Experience Advisor | S1 | Retail Banking | Scarborough
description:
Customer Experience Advisor | S1 | Retail Banking | ScarboroughCountry: United Kingdom

IT STARTS HERE


Santander () is evolving from a global, high-impact brand into a technology-driven organisation, and our people are at the heart of this journey. Together, we are driving a customer-centric transformation that values bold thinking, innovation, and the courage to challenge what’s possible.


This is more than a strategic shift. It’s a chance for driven professionals to grow, learn, and make a real difference.


Our mission is to contribute to help more people and businesses prosper. We embrace a strong risk culture and all our professionals at all levels are expected to take a proactive and responsible approach toward risk management.


Retail & Commercial Banking is a global business integrating all our retail and commercial banking activities to better serve our customers, improve efficiency and drive value creation.


THE DIFFERENCE YOU MAKE


Santander is looking for a Customer Experience Advisor based out of Scarborough Branch , working 35 hours per week, on a rota’d basis Monday to Saturday, between 8am & 6pm.


This Role is 12 Month Fixed Term Contract


For our customers, you’ll be more than just the friendly face and voice of Santander. You’ll be a listener and problem solver. Whether you’re helping someone with a simple cash transaction, aiding them with technology in the banking hall, transacting with them over the phone or protecting your customers against fraud and scams, you’ll never know what the next challenge will be.


What’s not in doubt is that you’ll have plenty of support. Life in a branch can be busy, varied and challenging, so we’re a close-knit team.


You’ll be totally flexible in your approach and comfortable in undertaking a broad range of activities. This means not limiting your time and focus on one particular element of your role. You’ll thrive on the variety this gives you and take satisfaction for operating in a multi-skilled environment. You’re the eyes and ears of our business after all.


We’re shaping the way we work through innovation, cutting-edge technology, collaboration and the freedom to explore new ideas. To succeed in this role, you will be responsible for:


  • Acting as the first point of contact for customers in branch or over the phone
  • Assisting with day-to-day transactions, queries and servicing
  • Answering customer calls into our contact centre
  • Building relationships and finding solutions
  • Developing your knowledge of services and products to help our customers
  • Identifying new ways to improve the customer experience

WHAT YOU’LL BRING


Our people are our greatest strength. Every individual contributes unique perspectives that make us stronger as a team and as an organisation. We’re enabling teams to go beyond by valuing who they are and empowering what they bring.


The following requirements represent the knowledge, skills, and abilities essential for success in this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


Professional Experience


  • Proven ability to deliver outstanding customer service either from a face to face or a telephony background (Required)
  • The ability to communicate effectively with customers to truly understand their needs (Required)
  • A real desire to go above-and-beyond for customers (Preferred)
  • Effective team working skills with a flexible, can-do approach to work (Preferred)
  • Openness to a broad range of activities even if outside of standard expectations (Preferred)
  • Ability to grow, adapt and change accommodating business needs and priorities (Preferred)

WE VALUE YOUR IMPACT


At Santander, your contribution matters. We recognise the difference you make every day, and we make sure you feel valued, supported and rewarded in return.


Here, recognition goes beyond pay. It’s about the pride you feel in your work, the impact you have on customers and communities, and the opportunities you have to grow and thrive — personally and professionally.


  • The starting salary is £25,000 together with a £500 flexible benefit allowance and the opportunity to earn a discretionary performance-related bonus of 8% of salary.
  • 25 days’ holiday plus bank holidays, which increases to 26 days after 5yrs service, with the option to purchase up to 5 contractual days per year.
  • Voluntary healthcare benefits at discounted rates. Including: medical insurance, dental insurance, and health assessments
  • We put 8% of salary into your pension, even if you don’t contribute yourself. We’ll pay in up to 12.5% of salary, if you contribute as well, and you can take some of our contribution in cash if you prefer.
  • Protection for you and your family, with company-funded death-in-service benefit and income protection insurance, and the option to take advantage of discounted rates for additional life assurance and critical illness cover.
  • Share in Santander’s success by saving or investing in our share plans.
  • As a Santander UK employee, you are able to request staff versions of our products like our Edge Current Accounts and Credit Cards with no fees, as well as apply to many other deals and discounts in Santander products and services
  • Competitive rewards that reflect the real impact you make and the value you bring.
  • Wellbeing that goes beyond work — we work with a range of wellbeing partners across our 4 pillars of wellbeing (physical, mental, social and financial) to give you access to a suite of apps, discounted gym and fitness access, weekly online classes, flexible healthcare and mental health support.
  • Support for every life stage — from menopause and pregnancy to parenthood and beyond, with enhanced family leave, childcare options and tailored wellbeing support.
  • Time to give back through volunteering opportunities that let you make a difference in the communities we serve.
  • Global growth opportunities to shape your career, learn new skills and explore what’s possible across our international network.

Ready to be recognised? It starts with you.


LOCAL COMPLIANCE


At Santander, we’re proud to be an inclusive organisation that provides equal opportunities for everyone — regardless of age, gender, disability, civil status, race, religion or sexual orientation.


We’re committed to creating a recruitment experience that’s accessible, fair and welcoming for all candidates.


We want our people to thrive — at work and at home — while delivering the best outcomes for our customers and supporting each other to grow.


When applying, please consider the travel distance, time and cost to your chosen Branch location.


Right to work in the UK


  • All candidates must have the right to work in the UK to commence employment with Santander.

WHAT TO DO NEXT


If this sounds like a role you are interested in, then please apply.


If there’s anything we can do in the recruitment process to help you achieve your best, get in touch. Whether it’s a copy of our application form in another format or additional assistance, we’re available through email. You can contact us at resourcing@santander.co.uk
